articles.title: Associative operations on self-maps
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a set and let $U$ be an operation that
assigns to any two maps $f, g \colon A \to A$ a map $U(f, g) \colon A \to A$. We say $U$ is
associative (condition (1) of Problem 171) if $U(f, U(g, h)) = U(U(f, g), h)$ for all maps
$f, g, h \colon A \to A$.

articles.title: Permutation-invariant operations on self-maps
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a set and let $U$ be an
operation that assigns to any two maps $f, g \colon A \to A$ a map $U(f, g) \colon A \to A$. We
say $U$ is invariant under permutations of $A$ (condition (2) of Problem 171) if conjugating the
arguments by a permutation conjugates the result: for every permutation $p$ of $A$ and all maps
$f, g \colon A \to A$, $U(p^{-1} \circ f \circ p, p^{-1} \circ g \circ p) = p^{-1} \circ U(f, g)
\circ p$.

articles.title: Scottish Book Problem 171 is false
articles.statement:
Not every associative, permutation-invariant operation
on self-maps is composition: there are a set $A$, an operation $U$ that assigns to any two maps
$f, g \colon A \to A$ a map $U(f, g) \colon A \to A$ and is both associative (condition (1) of
Problem 171) and invariant under permutations of $A$ (condition (2)), and maps
$f, g \colon A \to A$ with $U(f, g) \ne f \circ g$, where $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$.

Reverse composition $U(f, g) = g \circ f$ and the two projections $U(f, g) = f$ and
$U(f, g) = g$ satisfy (1) and (2) but are not composition in general. The typescript's
parenthetical $(U(f,g) \ne 1)$ is of unclear meaning and is not read as excluding these
counterexamples.

## Sources

- J. Schreier – S. Ulam, Problem 171 of the Scottish Book, typescript p. 76.

articles.title: Candido's identity
articles.statement:
For all elements $x$ and $y$ of a commutative semiring,
$2\left(x^4 + y^4 + (x + y)^4\right) = \left(x^2 + y^2 + (x + y)^2\right)^2$.

## Sources

- Kunle Adegoke, "Fibonacci Identities via Fibonacci Functions." <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL27/Adegoke/adegoke12.tex>, lines 826-833.

articles.title: Structure constants are bounded by one
articles.statement: A structure constant has absolute value at most one.

articles.title: Contractions of structure constants are bounded by one
articles.statement: A contraction of two structure constants has absolute value at most one.

articles.title: Sign cancellation for two decompositions of an xor index
articles.statement: The cancellation rule of signs for two distinct decompositions of one xor index.

articles.title: Basis multiplication signs square to one
articles.statement: Every basis multiplication sign squares to one.

articles.title: Sign of a product of octonion basis elements
articles.statement:
The sign of the product of basis elements indexed by `p` and `q`.

The output basis index is `p ^^^ q`. Bits are read least-significant first, so
bits 0, 1, and 2 correspond to the source coordinates 1, 2, and 3.

articles.title: Eight-square crossing identity
articles.statement: The two contractions in the eight-square crossing decomposition.

articles.title: Signed structure constant of the eight-square algebra
articles.statement: The signed structure constant for the basis product indexed by `p` and `q`.

articles.title: Contraction of two structure constants
articles.statement: Contracting two structure constants leaves their common xor component.

articles.title: Indicator function of a set
articles.statement:
For a set $A \subseteq \alpha$ and a type $R$ with a zero
and a one, the indicator function $\mathbb{1}_A : \alpha \to R$ takes the value $1$ at every
point of $A$ and the value $0$ at every point outside $A$.

articles.title: L-additive functions on a ring
articles.statement:
A function $f \colon K \to K$ on a ring $K$ is
L-additive when $f(mn) = f(m)\,n + f(n)\,m$ for all $m, n \in K$.

articles.title: Products regrouped by the values of a function
articles.statement:
Let $\beta$ and $\gamma$ be finite types,
let $M$ be a commutative monoid, and let $g : \beta \to \gamma$ and $f : \gamma \to M$. Then

$$\prod_{b \in \beta} f(g(b)) = \prod_{c \in \gamma} f(c)^{\#\{b \in \beta \mid g(b) = c\}},$$

where the product on the right runs over all of $\gamma$ and $\#\{b \in \beta \mid g(b) = c\}$ is
the number of elements $b$ of $\beta$ with $g(b) = c$.

articles.title: Amitsur–Levitzki theorem
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $n$ a natural number. For all
$n \times n$ matrices $M_1, \dots, M_{2n}$ over $R$, the sum over all permutations $\sigma$ of
$\{1, \dots, 2n\}$ of $\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma) M_{\sigma(1)} M_{\sigma(2)} \cdots M_{\sigma(2n)}$ is
the zero matrix, where $\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma) \in \{1, -1\}$ is the sign of $\sigma$. In other
words, the standard polynomial of degree $2n$ vanishes on $n \times n$ matrices over $R$.

## Sources

- A. S. Amitsur and J. Levitzki, Minimal identities for algebras, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 1 (1950), 449-463, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-1950-0036751-9; textbook in Rowen, Polynomial Identities in Ring Theory.

articles.title: Antipode of a commutative Hopf algebra is an involution
articles.statement: The antipode of a commutative Hopf algebra is an involution.

articles.title: Convolution inverse of an algebra homomorphism via the antipode
articles.statement:
Every algebra homomorphism from a possibly noncommutative Hopf algebra to a commutative
algebra has a convolution
inverse given by precomposition with the antipode.

articles.title: Convolution-power criterion for Hopf algebras
articles.statement: A compatibility corollary for the convolution-power criterion on Hopf algebras.

articles.title: Convolution-power criterion for bialgebras
articles.statement:
A convolution power is trivial on all points iff it is trivial on the
universal point.

articles.title: Algebra homomorphisms from a Hopf algebra are convolution units
articles.statement:
Algebra homomorphisms from a possibly noncommutative Hopf algebra to a commutative
algebra are convolution units.

articles.title: Comultiplication of the antipode
articles.statement: Comultiplication anticommutes with the antipode up to the tensor swap.

articles.title: Comultiplication commutes with the antipode when cocommutative
articles.statement:
In a cocommutative Hopf algebra, comultiplication commutes with the
antipode.

articles.title: Burnside's theorem on matrix algebras
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $n$ a natural
number, and $A$ a $k$-subalgebra of the algebra $M_n(k)$ of $n \times n$ matrices over $k$.
Suppose that the only subspaces $W$ of $k^n$ with $Mv \in W$ for all $M \in A$ and all $v \in W$
are $0$ and $k^n$. Then $A = M_n(k)$.

## Sources

- W. Burnside, On the condition of reducibility of any group of linear substitutions, Proc. London Math. Soc. 3 (1905), 430–434, DOI 10.1112/plms/s2-3.1.430; textbook in Lam, First Course in Noncommutative Rings, Thm 1.2. Burnside's theorem on matrix algebras / Burnside density.

articles.title: Frobenius theorem on real division algebras
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite-dimensional associative
unital division algebra over $\mathbb{R}$. Then $A$ is isomorphic as an $\mathbb{R}$-algebra to
$\mathbb{R}$, to $\mathbb{C}$, or to the algebra $\mathbb{H}$ of real quaternions.

## Sources

- G. Frobenius, Ueber lineare Substitutionen und bilineare Formen, J. reine angew. Math. 84 (1878), 1–63, DOI 10.1515/crelle-1878-18788403; textbook in Jacobson, Basic Algebra II; Lean states associative unital case via `DivisionRing` excluding octonions intentionally.

articles.title: m-system
articles.statement:
A subset $M$ of a ring $R$ is an $m$-system if it is nonempty, does not
contain $0$, and for all $a, b \in M$ there is some $r \in R$ with $a r b \in M$.

articles.title: Prime two-sided ideal
articles.statement:
A two-sided ideal $P$ of a ring $R$ is prime if $P \ne R$ and,
for all $a, b \in R$, if $a r b \in P$ for every $r \in R$, then $a \in P$ or $b \in P$.

This is the noncommutative notion of primality; being completely prime ($P \ne R$, and
$ab \in P$ forces $a \in P$ or $b \in P$) is stronger.

articles.title: Jacobson's commutativity theorem
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a ring. If for every $x \in R$ there is a
natural number $n > 1$ with $x^n = x$, then $R$ is commutative, that is, $xy = yx$ for all
$x, y \in R$.

articles.title: Köthe's conjecture is false
articles.statement:
There exist a ring $R$ (associative, with identity) and nil left
ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$ (left ideals all of whose elements are nilpotent) such that the sum
$I + J$ is not nil.

Adamczewski, Böhmler and Marczinzik (arXiv:2609.07996, 2026; Lean 4 machine-checked by
Adamczewski) build, over any countable field $F$, a nil algebra $N$ such that $M_2(F1 + N)$ has
two nil left ideals with non-nil sum. Greenfeld, King and Vendramin (arXiv:2609.15080) give an
independent refutation.

## Sources

- Tom Adamczewski, Bernhard Böhmler and René Marczinzik, A counterexample to Köthe's conjecture and a question of Rowen, arXiv:2609.07996 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.07996; Be'eri Greenfeld, G. King and Leandro Vendramin, The Köthe conjecture via point modules, arXiv:2609.15080 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.15080.

articles.title: Köthe's conjecture
articles.statement:
The statement that for every ring $R$ (associative, with identity)
and all nil left ideals $I$ and $J$ of $R$, the sum $I + J$ is again a nil left ideal.

articles.title: Nil left ideal
articles.statement:
A left ideal $I$ of a ring $R$ is nil if each of its elements is
nilpotent: for every $x \in I$ there is a natural number $n$ with $x^n = 0$.

articles.title: Skolem–Noether theorem
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finite-dimensional central
simple algebra over $k$. Then every $k$-algebra automorphism $\sigma$ of $A$ is inner: there is
a unit $u \in A^\times$ such that $\sigma(x) = u x u^{-1}$ for all $x \in A$.

## Sources

- T. Skolem, Zur Theorie der assoziativen Zahlensysteme, Skrifter Vidensk. Kristiania I (1927), no. 12; E. Noether, Nichtkommutative Algebra, Math. Z. 37 (1933), 514-541, DOI 10.1007/BF01474591.

articles.title: Anisotropy of the quaternion norm form reduces to a ternary form
articles.statement:
The quaternary norm form `x₀² - a·x₁² - b·x₂² + a·b·x₃²` of the
quaternion algebra `ℍ[K, a, b]` is anisotropic if and only if the ternary
form `z² - a·x² - b·y²` is. This equivalence also holds when either parameter
is zero; both forms are then isotropic.

This is the standard reduction of quaternion-algebra isotropy to a ternary
quadratic form. It is used to test whether a quaternion algebra is a
division algebra, in quadratic-form theory (anisotropy of Pfister forms),
and in local-global arguments for quaternion algebras.

articles.title: Quaternion algebras with isotropic norm form split
articles.statement:
If the norm form of a quaternion algebra over a field of characteristic
not two is isotropic, then the algebra splits: it is isomorphic to the
`2 × 2` matrix algebra.

articles.title: Ado–Iwasawa theorem
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra
over $K$. Then $L$ has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a
finite-dimensional vector space $V$ over $K$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over
$K$ from $L$ to the Lie algebra of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $V$ with the commutator bracket.

## Sources

- K. Iwasawa, On the representation of Lie algebras, Japanese Journal of Mathematics 19 (1948), 405–426. See also the Tau Ceti Ado–Iwasawa roadmap, https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCetiRoadmap/pull/102. Problem `adoIwasawa` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Ado's theorem
articles.statement:
Every finite-dimensional Lie algebra $L$ over a field $K$ of
characteristic zero has a faithful finite-dimensional representation: there are a natural
number $n$ and an injective homomorphism of Lie algebras over $K$ from $L$ into the Lie algebra
of $K$-linear endomorphisms of $K^n$ with the commutator bracket.

Proof: Following Tao's 2011 route, the nilpotent and solvable cases are proved by induction using
finite-dimensional quotients of universal enveloping algebras. The general case uses the Levi
decomposition and combines the resulting radical representation with the adjoint representation.

## Sources

- I. D. Ado, Bull. Soc. Phys.-Math. Kazan 7 (1935) and 1947 char-zero theorem; Bourbaki, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras; Lean states char-zero finite-dimensional version while modern theorem extends to arbitrary fields.

articles.title: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie
algebra over a field $K$ of characteristic zero, and let $M$ be a finite-dimensional Lie module
over $L$ and $K$. Then every Lie submodule $W$ of $M$ has a complement: there is a Lie submodule
$U$ of $M$ with $W \cap U = 0$ and $W + U = M$.

articles.title: Levi decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over a field $K$ of
characteristic zero, and let $\operatorname{rad}(L)$ be its radical, the largest solvable ideal
of $L$. Then there is a semisimple Lie subalgebra $S$ of $L$ (a Levi factor) such that
$L = \operatorname{rad}(L) \oplus S$ as $K$-vector spaces, that is,
$\operatorname{rad}(L) + S = L$ and $\operatorname{rad}(L) \cap S = 0$.

Proof: Weyl's complete reducibility theorem is proved with the trace-form Casimir operator. The
Levi factor is then constructed for an abelian radical and the general case follows by induction
through the derived ideal of the radical.

## Sources

- E. E. Levi, Atti Accad. Sci. Torino 1905 and A. I. Malcev, Izv. Akad. Nauk SSSR 1945; Bourbaki, Lie I; Lean states K-module direct sum form over char-zero fields.

articles.title: The zero ideal is a Poisson ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a
Poisson bracket. The zero ideal of $A$ is a Poisson ideal.

articles.title: Bracket with zero
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket
$\lbrace \cdot, \cdot \rbrace$. For every $a \in A$, $\lbrace a, 0 \rbrace = 0$.

articles.title: Poisson ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket
$\lbrace \cdot, \cdot \rbrace$. An ideal $P$ of $A$ is a Poisson ideal when
$\lbrace a, p \rbrace \in P$ for all $a \in A$ and all $p \in P$.

articles.title: Poisson prime ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket.
An ideal $P$ of $A$ is a Poisson prime when it is both a prime ideal and a Poisson ideal.

articles.title: Poisson ideals inside an ideal lie in its Poisson core
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
$\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket, and let $J$ and $P$ be ideals of $A$. If
$P \subseteq J$ and $P$ is a Poisson ideal, then $P$ is contained in the Poisson core of $J$.

articles.title: Poisson bracket
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra. A Poisson bracket on $A$
is a map assigning to $x, y \in A$ an element $\lbrace x, y \rbrace \in A$ such that for all
$x, y, z \in A$ and $c \in \mathbb{C}$: $\lbrace x + y, z \rbrace = \lbrace x, z \rbrace +
\lbrace y, z \rbrace$ and $\lbrace x, y + z \rbrace = \lbrace x, y \rbrace + \lbrace x, z \rbrace$;
$\lbrace x, y \rbrace = -\lbrace y, x \rbrace$; the Leibniz rule
$\lbrace x, yz \rbrace = y \lbrace x, z \rbrace + \lbrace x, y \rbrace z$ holds; the Jacobi
identity $\lbrace x, \lbrace y, z \rbrace \rbrace + \lbrace y, \lbrace z, x \rbrace \rbrace +
\lbrace z, \lbrace x, y \rbrace \rbrace = 0$ holds; and $\lbrace c x, y \rbrace =
c \lbrace x, y \rbrace$ and $\lbrace x, c y \rbrace = c \lbrace x, y \rbrace$.

articles.title: Universal property of the Poisson core
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra
with a Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is the greatest
element of the set of Poisson ideals of $A$ contained in $J$: it is a Poisson ideal contained in
$J$, and it contains every Poisson ideal of $A$ contained in $J$.

articles.title: The Poisson core is contained in the ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra
with a Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is contained in $J$.

articles.title: The Poisson core is a Poisson ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a
Poisson bracket. For every ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is a Poisson ideal.

The family of Poisson ideals contained in $J$ is nonempty and directed (the sum of two members
is again a member), so every element of the core lies in some member of the family.

articles.title: Poisson core
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket. For an
ideal $J$ of $A$, the Poisson core of $J$ is the supremum, in the lattice of ideals of $A$, of the
set of all Poisson ideals of $A$ contained in $J$.

It is the largest Poisson ideal contained in $J$ (universal property of the Poisson core).

articles.title: The sum of two Poisson ideals inside an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative
$\mathbb{C}$-algebra with a Poisson bracket, and let $I$, $K$ and $J$ be ideals of $A$. If $I$
and $K$ are Poisson ideals contained in $J$, then their sum $I + K$ is a Poisson ideal contained
in $J$.

articles.title: Rota–Baxter operators on groups
articles.statement:
A Rota–Baxter operator (of weight $1$) on a group $G$ is
a map $B \colon G \to G$ such that $B(g)\,B(h) = B\bigl(g\,B(g)\,h\,B(g)^{-1}\bigr)$ for all
$g, h \in G$.

articles.title: A surjective, non-injective Rota–Baxter operator on a non-abelian group
articles.statement:
There exist a
non-abelian group $G$ and a Rota–Baxter operator $B$ on $G$ that is surjective but not injective.

For example, van Doorn, Judin, Monticone and Morrison take $G = S_3 \times \mathbb{Z}^{\mathbb{N}}$
and $B(\sigma, f) = (\sigma^{-1}, s(f))$, where $s$ is the left shift.

## Sources

- E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Problem 20.125 (V. G. Bardakov); resolution: P. Monticone, Kourovka Notebook Problem 20.125, solution note, 23 March 2026; W. van Doorn, E. Judin, P. Monticone and D. Morrison, On some problems from the Kourovka Notebook, preprint, arXiv:2607.17477 (2026), van Doorn-Judin-Monticone-Morrison, Theorem 5.1: G = S3 × Z^N with B(σ, f) = (σ⁻¹, s(f)), s the left shift; the Kourovka Notebook (21st issue) marks 20.125 solved (AI solution confirmed by V. G. Bardakov), https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.17477.

articles.title: Kourovka Problem 20.125 (surjective non-injective Rota–Baxter operators)
articles.statement:
The statement,
asked by V. G. Bardakov, that there exist a non-abelian group $G$ and a Rota–Baxter operator $B$ on
$G$ such that $B$ is surjective but not injective.

articles.title: Class number of the holomorph of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
For every integer $n > 0$,
the number of conjugacy classes of the holomorph
$\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z} \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ equals
$\varphi(n) \sum_{d \mid n} 1/\varphi(d)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Theorem 23 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-thm-23`).

articles.title: Trivial center and automorphisms of the conjugation quandle
articles.statement:
For a group $G$, let
$\operatorname{Conj}(G)$ be the conjugation quandle on $G$, with $x \triangleleft y = x y x^{-1}$.
Then $G$ has trivial center if and only if the permutations of $G$ that are group automorphisms
are exactly the rack automorphisms of $\operatorname{Conj}(G)$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Lemma 17 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-lem-17`), quoting Bardakov, Nasybullov, and Singh, Corollary 2.

articles.title: Conjugacy in the holomorph of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$, let
$A = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, and write $(a, u)$ for the element of the holomorph
$A \rtimes A^\times$ with $a \in A$ and $u \in A^\times$. Two elements $(a, u)$ and $(b, v)$ are
conjugate if and only if $u = v$ and there is a unit $y \in A^\times$ with $b \equiv y a$ modulo
the ideal $(1 - u)A$ generated by $1 - u$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Proposition 22 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-prop-22`).

articles.title: Multiplication in the holomorph of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$A = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and write $(a, u)$ for the element of the holomorph
$A \rtimes A^\times$ with $a \in A$ and $u \in A^\times$. For all $a, b \in A$ and
$u, v \in A^\times$, $(a, u)(b, v) = (a + u b, u v)$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, proof of Proposition 22.

articles.title: Holomorph of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, let
$A = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$. The holomorph of $A$ is the semidirect product $A \rtimes A^\times$
in which the unit group $A^\times$ acts on $A$ by multiplication. Its elements are the pairs
$(a, u)$ with $a \in A$ and $u \in A^\times$, with product $(a, u)(b, v) = (a + u b, u v)$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 4.

articles.title: Affine maps are automorphisms of the dihedral quandle
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$,
every $a \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and every unit $u \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$, the
affine map $T_{a,u} \colon x \mapsto a + u x$ is a rack automorphism of the dihedral quandle
$R_n$, the set $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $x \triangleleft y = 2x - y$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 2.2 (virtual structures on the dihedral quandle).

articles.title: Affine permutations of the dihedral quandle
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, an element
$a \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and a unit $u \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$, $T_{a,u}$ is the
affine map $x \mapsto a + u x$ of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$, viewed as a permutation of the
dihedral quandle $R_n$ (the set $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $x \triangleleft y = 2x - y$).

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 2.2 (virtual structures on the dihedral quandle).

articles.title: Isomorphism of affine virtual dihedral quandles
articles.statement:
Let $n > 0$, let $R_n$ be the dihedral
quandle on $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ (with $x \triangleleft y = 2x - y$), and for
$a \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and $u \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ let $T_{a,u}$ be the
permutation $x \mapsto a + u x$ of $R_n$. For all $a, b \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and
$u, v \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$, the virtual racks $(R_n, T_{a,u})$ and
$(R_n, T_{b,v})$ are isomorphic if and only if $u = v$ and $b = y a + (1 - u) x$ for some
$x \in \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ and $y \in (\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Proposition 21 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-prop-21`).

articles.title: Automorphism group of a rack
articles.statement:
For a rack $R$ with operation $\triangleleft$, the
automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut} R$ is the subgroup of the group of permutations of $R$
consisting of the permutations $f$ with $f(x \triangleleft y) = f(x) \triangleleft f(y)$ for all
$x, y \in R$.

Here $x \triangleleft y$ is the paper's $s_x(y)$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 2.2 (rack homomorphisms and `Aut R`).

articles.title: Virtual quandle structures on the dihedral quandle
articles.statement:
For every $n > 0$, the number
$v(R_n)$ of isomorphism classes of virtual racks whose underlying rack is the dihedral quandle
$R_n$ (the set $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ with $x \triangleleft y = 2x - y$) equals
$\varphi(n) \sum_{d \mid n} 1/\varphi(d)$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Theorem 1 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-thm-1`).

articles.title: Number of isomorphism classes of virtual racks on a rack
articles.statement:
For a rack $R$, let
$\operatorname{Aut} R$ be its group of rack automorphisms; a virtual structure on $R$ is an
element $f \in \operatorname{Aut} R$, and $(R, f)$ is the corresponding virtual rack. The number
$v(R)$ is the number of classes of virtual structures on $R$, where $f, g \in \operatorname{Aut} R$
are identified when the virtual racks $(R, f)$ and $(R, g)$ are isomorphic; that is, the number
of isomorphism classes of virtual racks with underlying rack $R$. It is $0$ when there are
infinitely many classes.

Every virtual rack whose underlying rack is isomorphic to $R$ is isomorphic to one of the form
$(R, f)$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 3.2.2 (the invariant `v(R)`).

articles.title: Isomorphism of virtual structures is conjugacy
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a rack and let $f_1$ and $f_2$
be elements of its automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut} R$. Then the virtual racks $(R, f_1)$
and $(R, f_2)$ are isomorphic if and only if $f_1$ and $f_2$ are conjugate in
$\operatorname{Aut} R$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Proposition 14 (`jis-2025-25.8.4-prop-14`).

articles.title: Reflexivity of virtual rack isomorphism
articles.statement:
For every rack $R$ and every permutation $f$ of
$R$, the pair $(R, f)$ is isomorphic to itself in the sense of virtual rack isomorphism. The
permutation $f$ need not be a rack automorphism.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 2.2 (virtual rack isomorphisms).

articles.title: Isomorphism of virtual racks
articles.statement:
Write $x \triangleleft y$ for the operation of a rack. A
virtual rack $(R, f)$ is a rack $R$ together with a rack automorphism $f$ of $R$, its virtual
structure. Let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be racks and let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be permutations of $R_1$ and
$R_2$. Then $(R_1, f_1)$ and $(R_2, f_2)$ are isomorphic when there is a bijection
$\psi \colon R_1 \to R_2$ such that $\psi(x \triangleleft y) = \psi(x) \triangleleft \psi(y)$
for all $x, y \in R_1$ and $\psi(f_1(x)) = f_2(\psi(x))$ for all $x \in R_1$.

The definition does not require $f_1$ and $f_2$ to be rack automorphisms; for virtual racks it
is the usual notion of isomorphism.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 2.2 (virtual rack isomorphisms).

articles.title: Multiplication action of the units of $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$
articles.statement:
For a natural number
$n$, the group homomorphism from the unit group $(\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z})^\times$ to the
automorphism group of the additive group $\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ that sends a unit $u$ to
multiplication by $u$, the automorphism $x \mapsto u x$.

## Sources

- Lực Ta, *Enumeration of Virtual Quandles Up to Isomorphism*, Journal of Integer Sequences 28 (2025), Article 25.8.4, Section 4 (the holomorph `A ⋊ A^×`, `A = ℤ/nℤ`).

articles.title: Dimension of a multihomogeneous component of a free Lie algebra
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field and
let $n_1, \dots, n_r$ be natural numbers with $n_1 + \dots + n_r > 0$. Then the multihomogeneous
component of multidegree $(n_1, \dots, n_r)$ of the free Lie algebra over $K$ on $r$ generators
has dimension over $K$ equal to Witt's multigraded value $M(n_1, \dots, n_r)$.

articles.title: Multihomogeneous components of a free Lie algebra
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $r$ a natural
number, and $L$ the free Lie algebra over $K$ on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{r-1}$. For a
multidegree $d \in \mathbb{N}^r$, the multihomogeneous component of $L$ of multidegree $d$ is the
$K$-linear span of the homogeneous Lie monomials of multidegree $d$, that is, of the iterated
brackets of the generators in which each $x_i$ occurs exactly $d_i$ times.

These components distinguish multidegrees, not only the total bracket length.

## Sources

- Pieter Moree, *Convoluted Convolved Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 7 (2004), Article 04.2.2, Witt's formula paragraph (the subspace `H` generated by homogeneous elements of multidegree `(n₁, …, nᵣ)`), lines 621–628, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL7/Moree/moree12.tex>.

articles.title: Free Lie monomials
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $r$ a natural number, and $L$ the free Lie algebra
over $K$ on generators $x_0, \dots, x_{r-1}$. The relation "$x$ is a homogeneous Lie monomial of
multidegree $d$", for $d \in \mathbb{N}^r$ and $x \in L$, is defined inductively: each generator
$x_i$ is a monomial of multidegree $e_i$, which is $1$ at $i$ and $0$ elsewhere; and if $x$ is a
monomial of multidegree $a$ and $y$ is a monomial of multidegree $b$, then the bracket $[x, y]$
is a monomial of multidegree $a + b$, computed pointwise. There are no other monomials.

articles.title: Witt's multigraded dimension formula
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field, let $r > 0$, and let
$n_1, \dots, n_r$ be natural numbers with $n_1 + \dots + n_r > 0$. Then the multihomogeneous
component of multidegree $(n_1, \dots, n_r)$ of the free Lie algebra over $K$ on $r$ generators
has dimension over $K$ equal to Witt's multigraded value $M(n_1, \dots, n_r)$.

Proof: The Lyndon-word basis identifies the component with the Lyndon words of
the prescribed content, which are counted by Möbius inversion.

## Sources

- Pieter Moree, *Convoluted Convolved Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 7 (2004), Article 04.2.2, Witt's formula paragraph, lines 621–628, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL7/Moree/moree12.tex>.

articles.title: Witt's multigraded value
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n_1, \dots, n_r$, let
$n = n_1 + \dots + n_r$ and $g = \gcd(n_1, \dots, n_r)$. The rational number
$M(n_1, \dots, n_r)$ is $0$ if $n = 0$, and otherwise
$M(n_1, \dots, n_r) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{d \mid g} \mu(d) \binom{n/d}{n_1/d, \ldots, n_r/d}$,
where the sum runs over the positive divisors $d$ of $g$, $\mu$ is the Möbius function, and the
last factor is the multinomial coefficient of $n_1/d, \dots, n_r/d$.

## Sources

- Pieter Moree, *Convoluted Convolved Fibonacci Numbers*, Journal of Integer Sequences 7 (2004), Article 04.2.2, equations `witty`/`basaal`, lines 598–613 (Möbius inversion of the circular-word count; context *Circular words and Witt's dimension formula*, lines 574–597), <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL7/Moree/moree12.tex>.

articles.title: Binomial theorem for rising factorials
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$ and all real numbers
$a$ and $b$, writing $x^{\overline{m}} = x(x+1)\cdots(x+m-1)$ for the rising factorial,

$$(a+b)^{\overline{n}} = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, a^{\overline{k}}\, b^{\overline{n-k}}.$$

## Sources

- Paul Eloe and Catherine Kublik, "When Numerical Analysis Crosses Paths with Catalan and Generalized Motzkin Numbers," Journal of Integer Sequences 21 (2018), Article 18.8.4, Theorem, equation, lines 156–161, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL21/Kublik/kublik2.tex

articles.title: Explicit formula for the Bessel polynomials
articles.statement:
For every natural number $n$, the Bessel
polynomial $y_n \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ equals
$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{(n+k)!}{2^k \, k! \, (n-k)!} \, x^k$.

This is the defining formula, so the identity holds by definition.

## Sources

- Schork, lines 285-288.

articles.title: The first Bessel polynomial
articles.statement:
The Bessel polynomial $y_1$ equals $1 + x$.

## Sources

- Schork, lines 285-288.

articles.title: The second Bessel polynomial
articles.statement:
The Bessel polynomial $y_2$ equals $1 + 3x + 3x^2$.

## Sources

- Schork, lines 285-288.

articles.title: The zeroth Bessel polynomial
articles.statement:
The Bessel polynomial $y_0$ is the constant
polynomial $1$.

## Sources

- Schork, lines 285-288.

articles.title: Bessel polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the $n$-th classical Bessel polynomial
$y_n$ is the polynomial with rational coefficients
$y_n(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \frac{(n+k)!}{2^k \, k! \, (n-k)!} \, x^k$.

## Sources

- Schork, lines 285-288.

articles.title: Splitting the numerator of a unified Catalan-type generating function
articles.statement:
Let
$j, k, m, d, n$ be natural numbers, let $a, b, c, \lambda, x, y$ be real numbers and let $A$ be
a polynomial with integer coefficients. Let $K(t)$ be the negative real power of the trinomial
$c - a x t + b (2x - 1)^d t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as a power series in $t$ (for $c > 0$ and
$m \ge 1$ this is the expansion of $(c - a x t + b (2x - 1)^d t^m)^{-\lambda}$ in powers of $t$),
and let $S(t) = \sum_i y^i t^i / i!$, the sum running over the natural numbers $i \ge k$ with
$j \mid i - k$ (for $j \ge 1$ this is the pseudo-Bessel function $S(j, k, yt)$ of Equation (5)).
Then the coefficient of $t^n$ in $(S(t) + A(x)\, t)\, K(t)$ equals the coefficient of $t^n$ in
$S(t) K(t)$, plus the coefficient of $t^n$ in $(1 + A(x)\, t)\, K(t)$, minus the coefficient of
$t^n$ in $K(t)$.

In the paper's notation this is
$P^{j.k;\lambda,A}_{n,m}(x, y) = P^{j.k;\lambda,0}_{n,m}(x, y) + P^{1.0;\lambda,A}_{n,m}(x) -
P^{1.0;\lambda,0}_{n,m}(x)$; the kernel is the paper's for $c > 0$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Theorem 6.

articles.title: Hermite-shifted Catalan-type polynomials as convolutions
articles.statement:
Write $H_n(x, y) = H^2_n(x, y)$
for the Kampé de Fériet polynomials. For a natural number $m$ and real numbers $\lambda, z$,
write $(1 - m t + z t^m)^{-\lambda}$ and $(1 - m z t + t^m)^{-\lambda}$ for the negative real
powers of the trinomials $1 - m t + z t^m$ and $1 - m z t + t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as
power series in $t$ (for $m \ge 1$ these are their expansions in powers of $t$), and let
$P^\lambda_{r,m}(z)$ and $h^\lambda_{r,m}(z)$ be their coefficients of $t^r$. For all natural
numbers $k, m, n$ and real numbers $\lambda, x, y, z$, as formal power series in $t$ (with
$e^{xt + yt^2}$ the exponential series and $H_k(x + 2yt, y)$ evaluated in power series), the
coefficient of $t^n$ in $e^{xt + yt^2} H_k(x + 2yt, y) (1 - m t + z t^m)^{-\lambda}$ is
$\sum_{r=0}^{n} H_{n-r+k}(x, y) P^\lambda_{r,m}(z) / (n - r)!$, and the coefficient of $t^n$
in $e^{xt + yt^2} H_k(x + 2yt, y) (1 - m z t + t^m)^{-\lambda}$ is
$\sum_{r=0}^{n} H_{n-r+k}(x, y) h^\lambda_{r,m}(z) / (n - r)!$.

These coefficients are the paper's $H^{k;\lambda}_{n,m}(x, y, z)$ and
$h^{k;\lambda}_{n,m}(x, y, z)$ (Definition 3, Equations (8) and (9)).

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Nieto–Hermite Catalan-type polynomials as convolutions
articles.statement:
Let $j, k, m, r$ be natural
numbers with $k \le r$ and let $\lambda, x, y$ be real numbers. Let $E(t) = e^{2yt - t^2}$ be the
exponential series, so that its coefficient of $t^n$ is $H_n(y) / n!$ with $H_n$ the Hermite
polynomials, and let $F(t)$ be the power series whose coefficient of $t^n$ is $H_n(y) / n!$ when
$n \ge k$ and $j \mid n - k$, and $0$ otherwise (for $j \ge 1$ this is the series
$F(j, k, y, t) = \sum_n H_{jn+k}(y) t^{jn+k} / (jn + k)!$ of Equation (1)). Write
$(1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$ and $(1 - m x t + t^m)^{-\lambda}$ for the negative real powers
of the trinomials $1 - m t + x t^m$ and $1 - m x t + t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as power
series in $t$ (for $m \ge 1$ these are their expansions in powers of $t$), let
$P^\lambda_{s,m}(x)$ and $h^\lambda_{s,m}(x)$ be their coefficients of $t^s$, and let
$q = \lfloor (r - k) / j \rfloor$, read as $q = 0$ when $j = 0$. Then the coefficient of
$t^r$ in $F(t) (1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$ is
$\sum_{n=0}^{q} H_{jn+k}(y) P^\lambda_{r-jn-k,m}(x) / (jn + k)!$, and the coefficient of $t^r$
in $F(t) (1 - m x t + t^m)^{-\lambda}$ is the same sum with $h^\lambda_{r-jn-k,m}(x)$ in place
of $P^\lambda_{r-jn-k,m}(x)$.

These are the paper's $F^{j.k;\lambda}_{r,m}(x, y)$ and $f^{j.k;\lambda}_{r,m}(x, y)$
(Equations (10) and (11)). The paper takes $j, m \ge 1$; for $r < k$ its sum is empty.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Theorem 3.

articles.title: Constant term of the trinomial series
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $\lambda, c, \alpha, \beta$
and every natural number $m \ne 0$, the negative real power of the trinomial
$c - \alpha t + \beta t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as a power series in $t$, that is, the real
power $c^{-\lambda}$ times the binomial series $(1 + u)^{-\lambda}$ with
$u = (-\alpha t + \beta t^m)/c$ substituted (where $u = 0$ when $c = 0$), has constant term
$c^{-\lambda}$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equation (6).

articles.title: Hankel determinants of recurrent Catalan-type sequences vanish
articles.statement:
Let $m, N, r$ be natural
numbers with $r \le N$, let $\lambda, x$ be real numbers, let $A$ be a polynomial with integer
coefficients, and let $P_n$ be the coefficient of $t^n$ in
$(1 + A(x)\, t)(1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$, where $(1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$ denotes the
negative real power of the trinomial $1 - m t + x t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as a power series
in $t$ (for $m \ge 1$, its expansion in powers of $t$). Suppose real numbers $c_0, \dots, c_r$,
not all zero, satisfy $\sum_{k=0}^{r} c_k P_{n-k} = 0$ for every $n \ge r$. Then the
$(N + 1) \times (N + 1)$ Hankel matrix with $(i, j)$ entry $P_{i+j}$ for $0 \le i, j \le N$ has
determinant $0$.

In the paper's notation $P_n = P^{\lambda,A}_{n,m}(x)$, the recurrence is Equation (22) and the
Hankel matrix is $H_N^{(m,\lambda,A)}(x)$ of Equation (20). The paper's assumption $1 \le r$ is
dropped.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Theorem 8.

articles.title: Determinant of the lower-triangular Catalan-type matrix
articles.statement:
Let $m, N$ be natural numbers,
let $\lambda, x$ be real numbers, let $A$ be a polynomial with integer coefficients, and let
$P_n$ be the coefficient of $t^n$ in $(1 + A(x)\, t)(1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$, where
$(1 - m t + x t^m)^{-\lambda}$ denotes the negative real power of the trinomial
$1 - m t + x t^m$ with exponent $\lambda$ as a power series in $t$ (for $m \ge 1$, its expansion
in powers of $t$). Then the $(N + 1) \times (N + 1)$ matrix whose $(i, j)$ entry, for
$0 \le i, j \le N$, is $P_{i-j}$ when $j \le i$ and $0$ otherwise has determinant $P_0^{N+1}$.

In the paper's notation $P_n = P^{\lambda,A}_{n,m}(x)$ (Definition 6 at $y = 0$) and the matrix
is $P_N^{(m,\lambda,A)}(x)$ of Equation (18). The paper's proviso $P_0 \ne 0$ is dropped.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Theorem 7.

articles.title: The second Kampé de Fériet polynomial
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $x$ and $y$,
$H^2_2(x, y) = x^2 + 2y$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equation (2).

articles.title: The zeroth Kampé de Fériet polynomial
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m$ and all elements
$x, y$ of a commutative $\mathbb{R}$-algebra, $H^m_0(x, y) = 1$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equation (2).

articles.title: Kampé de Fériet polynomials
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $m, n$ and elements $x, y$ of a
commutative $\mathbb{R}$-algebra, the Kampé de Fériet (two-variable Hermite) polynomial is

$$H^m_n(x, y) = \sum_{r=0}^{q} \frac{n!}{r!\,(n - m r)!}\, y^r x^{n - m r},$$

where $q = \lfloor n / m \rfloor$, read as $q = 0$ when $m = 0$. The paper writes $H_n(x, y)$
for $H^2_n(x, y)$; taking values in an algebra lets $H_k(x + 2yt, y)$ be formed as a formal
power series in $t$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equation (2).

articles.title: The trinomial series at exponent one
articles.statement:
For all real numbers $\alpha, \beta$ and every
natural number $m \ne 0$, the formal expansion of $(1 - \alpha t + \beta t^m)^{-\lambda}$ in
powers of $t$ at $\lambda = -1$ is the polynomial $1 - \alpha t + \beta t^m$ itself.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equation (6).

articles.title: Negative real power of a trinomial as a power series
articles.statement:
For real numbers $\lambda$, $c$,
$\alpha$, $\beta$ and a natural number $m$, this is the formal power series in $t$ with real
coefficients

$$c^{-\lambda} \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{-\lambda}{n} u^n, \qquad u = \frac{-\alpha t + \beta t^m}{c},$$

that is, the real power $c^{-\lambda}$ times the binomial series
$(1 + t)^{-\lambda} = \sum_{n \ge 0} \binom{-\lambda}{n} t^n$ with $u$ substituted for $t$ (for
$c = 0$ the division is read as $0$, so $u = 0$). The substitution is meaningful when $u$ has
zero constant term, which holds for $m \ge 1$; for $c > 0$ and $m \ge 1$ the series is the
expansion of $(c - \alpha t + \beta t^m)^{-\lambda}$ in powers of $t$.

For $c > 0$ and $m \ge 1$ this is the denominator factor of every generating function in Pathan
and Usman's paper; Section 2 takes $c = 1$, $\alpha = m$ and $\beta = x$.

## Sources

- M. A. Pathan and T. Usman, *Unified Catalan-Type Polynomials with Matrix Formulations and Applications*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A105, Equations (6), (12) and (15).

articles.title: Coefficients of the unsigned Charlier polynomials
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $n$ and $m$,
the coefficient of $x^m$ in the $n$-th unsigned Charlier polynomial of order $0$ over $\mathbb{N}$
equals the unsigned Charlier coefficient $c(n, m)$.

articles.title: Unsigned Charlier coefficient
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the unsigned Charlier
coefficient is the natural number

$$c(n, m) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, [x^m]\, x^{\overline{k}},$$

where $x^{\overline{k}} = x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ is the rising factorial polynomial over
$\mathbb{N}$ and $[x^m]$ denotes the coefficient of $x^m$.

articles.title: Unsigned Charlier polynomials of order 0
articles.statement:
For a semiring $R$ and a natural number $n$,
the $n$-th unsigned Charlier polynomial of order $0$ is

$$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k}\, x^{\overline{k}} \in R[x],$$

where $x^{\overline{k}} = x(x+1)\cdots(x+k-1)$ is the rising factorial polynomial.

It is the terminating hypergeometric series ${}_2F_0(-n, x; ; -1)$, an unsigned version of the
Charlier polynomials of order 0, and its coefficient array is the exponential Riordan array
$[e^x, \ln(1/(1-x))]$.

articles.title: Coefficients of the Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind
articles.statement:
Let $U_n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$
denote the $n$-th Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind, and let $k \le n$ be natural numbers.
If $n$ and $k$ have the same parity, the coefficient of $x^k$ in $U_n$ is
$(-1)^{(n-k)/2} \sum_{i=0}^{k} \binom{(n+k)/2}{i} \binom{(n+k)/2 - i}{(n-k)/2}$;
otherwise it is $0$.

## Sources

- Milan Janjić, "On a Class of Polynomials with Integer Coefficients", Journal of Integer Sequences 11 (2008), Article 08.5.2, Corollary lines 441-446, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL11/Janjic/janjic19.tex>.

articles.title: Modified Chebyshev base polynomials of the second kind
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$ and
$r, s \in R$, the polynomials $P_n \in R[x]$, $n \ge 0$, are defined by $P_0 = 1$,
$P_1 = x - r$ and $P_{n+2} = (x - r) P_{n+1} - s P_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.

articles.title: Three-term recurrence for generalized Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$,
all $r, s, \lambda, \mu \in R$ and every $n \ge 0$, the generalized Chebyshev polynomials of
the second kind $Q_n \in R[x]$ with parameters $r, s, \lambda, \mu$ satisfy
$Q_{n+3} = (x - r) Q_{n+2} - s Q_{n+1}$.

No hypothesis on $\mu$ is needed because the recurrence starts at $Q_3$; the analogous
identity $Q_2 = (x - r) Q_1 - s Q_0$ holds only when $\mu = 0$.

articles.title: Generalized Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind
articles.statement:
For a commutative ring $R$ and
$r, s, \lambda, \mu \in R$, let $P_n \in R[x]$ be the modified Chebyshev base polynomials
with parameters $r, s$. The polynomials $Q_n \in R[x]$ are defined by $Q_0 = 1$,
$Q_1 = P_1 - \lambda P_0$ and $Q_{n+2} = P_{n+2} - \lambda P_{n+1} - \mu P_n$
for every $n \ge 0$.

articles.title: Classical orthogonal polynomial family
articles.statement:
A classical orthogonal polynomial family consists
of real polynomials $P_0, P_1, P_2, \dots$, each $P_n$ monic of degree exactly $n$, a measure
$\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$, a measurable set $D \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ that is an interval with
nonempty interior, and a function $w : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ (the weight), such that
$w(x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in D$; $\mu$ is the measure with density $w$ with respect to
Lebesgue measure restricted to $D$; $\int P_m P_n \, d\mu = 0$ whenever $m \ne n$;
$\int P_n^2 \, d\mu \ne 0$ for every $n$; and there are real numbers $u_0, u_1, v_0, v_1, v_2$,
with $v_0, v_1, v_2$ not all zero, such that at every interior point $x$ of $D$ the weight is
differentiable and $(v_0 + v_1 x + v_2 x^2) \, w'(x) = (u_0 + u_1 x) \, w(x)$ (the Pearson
equation).

articles.title: Favard's theorem, forward direction
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a
formally orthogonal family of monic polynomials over $R$. Then there are sequences
$(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$
such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and
$p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Barry, JIS VOL14 (`Barry1/barry97r2.tex`), lines 346-352. URL: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Barry1/barry97r2.tex

articles.title: Favard's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a field and let $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be a family of monic
polynomials in $R[x]$. Then $(p_n)$ is formally orthogonal if and only if there are sequences
$(\alpha_n)_{n \ge 0}$ and $(\beta_n)_{n \ge 0}$ in $R$ with $\beta_n \ne 0$ for all $n \ge 1$
such that $p_0 = 1$, $p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, and
$p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) \, p_n - \beta_n \, p_{n-1}$ for all $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- Paul Barry, "Riordan Arrays, Orthogonal Polynomials as Moments, and Hankel Transforms," Journal of Integer Sequences 14 (2011), Article 11.2.2, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Barry1/barry97r2.tex, Favard theorem at lines 346–352.

articles.title: Formally orthogonal polynomial family
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a field. A family $(p_n)_{n \ge 0}$ of
polynomials over $R$ is formally orthogonal if there is an $R$-linear functional
$L \colon R[x] \to R$ such that each $p_n$ has degree $n$, $L(p_n p_m) = 0$ whenever $n \ne m$,
and $L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ for every $n$.

## Sources

- Barry, JIS VOL14 (`Barry1/barry97r2.tex`), lines 326-331. URL: https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL14/Barry1/barry97r2.tex

articles.title: Trace formula for the monic Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $\bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be
the monic Chebyshev polynomials, given by $\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$ and
$\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$, and let $M$ be the $2 \times 2$ matrix over
$\mathbb{Z}[X]$ with rows $(X, -1)$ and $(1, 0)$. Then $\bar T_k = \operatorname{tr}(M^k)$ for
every natural number $k$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 3.2 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-7`).

articles.title: Positivity of the monic Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $\bar T_k \in \mathbb{R}[X]$ be the
monic Chebyshev polynomials, given by $\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$ and
$\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$. Then $\bar T_k(x) > 0$ for every natural number $k$
and every real number $x \ge 2$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 3.1 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-6`).

articles.title: Binomial expansion of the partial sums of Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
For every $n \ge 1$,

$$F_n = \sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor n/2 \rfloor} (-1)^m \binom{n-m}{m} X^{n-2m} +
\sum_{m=0}^{\lfloor (n-1)/2 \rfloor} (-1)^m \binom{n-m-1}{m} X^{n-2m-1}.$$

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 3.4 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-9`).

articles.title: Generating function of the partial sums of Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
In the ring $\mathbb{Z}[X][[t]]$ of formal power series in $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}[X]$,

$$(1 - X t + t^2) \sum_{n \ge 0} F_n t^n = 1 + t.$$

Since $1 - X t + t^2$ is a unit in $\mathbb{Z}[X][[t]]$, this is equivalent to
$\sum_{n \ge 0} F_n t^n = (1 + t)/(1 - X t + t^2)$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 3.3 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-8`).

articles.title: Laurent polynomial identity for the partial sums of Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_r = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{r} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
For every natural number $r$, in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$ of Laurent polynomials,

$$q^{r+1} + q^{-r-1} - q^r - q^{-r} = q^{-1} (q - 1)^2 F_r(q + q^{-1}).$$

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Lemma 6.1 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-lem-26`).

articles.title: First and second partial sums of the Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
Then $F_1 = X + 1$ and $F_2 = X^2 + X - 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Table 4.

articles.title: Three-term recurrence for the partial sums of Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
For every $k \ge 1$, $F_{k+1} = X F_k - F_{k-1}$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 3.6 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-11`).

articles.title: Successive partial sums of the Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
For every natural number $n$, $F_{n+1} = F_n + \bar T_{n+1}$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, (3.6).

articles.title: Leading coefficients of the partial sums of Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
For every $n \ge 5$, the polynomial

$$F_n - \Big(X^n + X^{n-1} - (n-1) X^{n-2} - (n-2) X^{n-3} + \binom{n-2}{2} X^{n-4} +
\binom{n-3}{2} X^{n-5}\Big)$$

is either zero or has degree less than $n - 5$.

Here $\binom{n-2}{2} = (n-2)(n-3)/2$ and $\binom{n-3}{2} = (n-3)(n-4)/2$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Corollary 3.5 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-cor-10`).

articles.title: Zeroth partial sum of the Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$F_n = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be the partial sums of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$ ($\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$, $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$).
Then $F_0 = 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, (3.6).

articles.title: Partial sums of the monic Chebyshev polynomials
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 0$, $F_n(X)$ is the
polynomial with integer coefficients

$$F_n(X) = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n} \bar T_k(X),$$

where $\bar T_k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is the monic Chebyshev polynomial of the source, that is, the
polynomial with $\bar T_k(q + q^{-1}) = q^k + q^{-k}$; equivalently $\bar T_0 = 2$,
$\bar T_1 = X$ and $\bar T_{k+2} = X \bar T_{k+1} - \bar T_k$. Thus $F_0 = 1$ and
$F_n = F_{n-1} + \bar T_n$ for $n \ge 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, (3.6)–(3.7).

articles.title: Zeta function of the Hilbert scheme of points on the two-dimensional torus
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime, $k \ge 1$, $q = p^k$ and $n \ge 1$. For $m \ge 1$ let $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$ be the field with
$q^m$ elements and let $N_m$ be the number of ideals $I$ of the Laurent polynomial ring
$\mathbb{F}_{q^m}[x^{\pm 1}, y^{\pm 1}]$ (the group algebra of $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}$)
such that the quotient by $I$ has dimension $n$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$; this is the number of
$\mathbb{F}_{q^m}$-points of the Hilbert scheme $H^n$ of $n$ points on the torus. For an odd
divisor $d$ of $n$ put $r_n(d) = n/d - (d + 1)/2$, $a_d = n + r_n(d)$ and $b_d = n - r_n(d)$.
Then the zeta function $Z(t) = \exp\big(\sum_{m \ge 1} N_m t^m / m\big)$, a formal power series
with rational coefficients, is

$$Z(t) = \prod_{d} \frac{(1-q^{a_d}t)(1-q^{b_d}t)}{(1-q^{a_d+1}t)(1-q^{b_d-1}t)},$$

the product running over the odd divisors $d$ of $n$.

The exponents $a_d$, $b_d$, $a_d + 1$ and $b_d - 1$ are nonnegative integers.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 5.5 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-25`).

articles.title: The absolute coefficient sum of $C_n$ counts odd divisors
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let $\bar P_n$ be
the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial, and write $C_n(q)/q^n$ for the Laurent polynomial
$(q - 2 + q^{-1})\,\bar P_n(q + q^{-1})$ in $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$. Then the sum of the absolute
values of the coefficients of $C_n(q)/q^n$ equals four times the number of odd divisors of $n$.

Multiplying by $q^n$ does not change the coefficients, so this is the source's statement about
the polynomial $C_n(q)$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Corollary 5.4 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-cor-24`).

articles.title: $C_n(q)/q^n$ as a sum over the solutions of $h(h + 1 + 2a) = 2n$
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let
$\bar P_n$ be the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial, and write $C_n(q)/q^n$ for the Laurent polynomial
$(q - 2 + q^{-1})\,\bar P_n(q + q^{-1})$ in $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$. Then

$$\frac{C_n(q)}{q^n} = \sum_{(h, a)} (-1)^h \left(q^a + q^{-a}\right),$$

where the sum runs over the pairs of integers $(h, a)$ with $1 \le h \le 2n$, $-n \le a \le n$
and $h(h + 1 + 2a) = 2n$. Moreover, if $h, h'$ are positive integers and $a, a'$ are
integers with $h(h + 1 + 2a) = 2n$, $h'(h' + 1 + 2a') = 2n$ and $|a| = |a'|$, then $h = h'$
and $a = a'$.

Every pair of integers $(h, a)$ with $h \ge 1$ and $h(h + 1 + 2a) = 2n$ satisfies $h \le 2n$
and $|a| \le n$, so the sum runs over all such pairs.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Lemma 5.2 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-lem-22`).

articles.title: Increasing-sequence and odd-divisor formulas for $C_n(q)/q^n$
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let
$\bar P_n$ be the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial, and write $C_n(q)/q^n$ for the Laurent polynomial
$(q - 2 + q^{-1})\,\bar P_n(q + q^{-1})$ in $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$. For integers $h \ge 1$ and
$a$ let $IS(a, h) = \{a + 1, \dots, a + h\}$.

(i) We have

$$\frac{C_n(q)}{q^n} = \sum_{(h, a)} (-1)^h \left(q^a + q^{-a}\right),$$

where the sum runs over the pairs of integers $(h, a)$ with $1 \le h \le 2n$ and $-n \le a \le n$
such that the elements of $IS(a, h)$ sum to $n$. Moreover, if $h, h' \ge 1$ and $a, a'$ are
integers such that the elements of $IS(a, h)$ and those of $IS(a', h')$ both sum to $n$, and
$|a| = |a'|$, then $h = h'$ and $a = a'$.

(ii) For an odd divisor $d$ of $n$ put $u_d = n/d - (d - 1)/2$ and $v_d = n/d - (d + 1)/2$. Then

$$\frac{C_n(q)}{q^n} = \sum_{d \mid n,\ d \text{ odd}} (q^{u_d} + q^{-u_d} - q^{v_d} - q^{-v_d}),$$

and in the list of the exponents $u_d, -u_d, v_d, -v_d$ over all odd divisors $d$ of $n$, the
nonzero entries are pairwise distinct.

Every pair $(h, a)$ with $h \ge 1$ such that the elements of $IS(a, h)$ sum to $n$ satisfies
$h \le 2n$ and $|a| \le n$, so the sum in (i) runs over all such sequences.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Theorem 5.3 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-thm-23`).

articles.title: The top coefficients $a_{n,i}$ equal $1$
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and let $i$ be a natural number
with $n \le 2i + 2$ and $i \le n - 1$; equivalently $n/2 - 1 \le i \le n - 1$, where $n/2$ is
the rational number, not the integer quotient. Then the Kassel–Reutenauer coefficient $a_{n,i}$
equals $1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Lemma 4.3 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-lem-14`).

articles.title: Small values of the coefficients $a_{n,i}$
articles.statement:
The Kassel–Reutenauer coefficients satisfy
$a_{1,0} = 1$, $a_{2,0} = a_{2,1} = 1$, $a_{3,0} = 0$ and $a_{3,1} = a_{3,2} = 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, (2.3) and Table 2.

articles.title: The Kassel–Reutenauer coefficients $a_{n,i}$
articles.statement:
For natural numbers $n$ and $i$, $a_{n,i}$ is
the number of positive divisors $d$ of $n$ with

$$\frac{i + \sqrt{2n + i^2}}{2} < d \le i + \sqrt{2n + i^2},$$

equivalently with $d(d - 2i) \le 2n$ and $n < 2d(d - i)$. For $n = 0$ the set of divisors is
taken to be empty, so $a_{0,i} = 0$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, display (2.3), quoting their earlier Theorem 1.3 of *Complete determination of the zeta function of the Hilbert scheme of n points on a two-dimensional torus*.

articles.title: Integers at which $|\bar P_n|$ is multiplicative
articles.statement:
Let $\bar P_n$ be the
Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial and let $N$ be an integer. Then
$|\bar P_{mn}(N)| = |\bar P_m(N)|\,|\bar P_n(N)|$ for all coprime positive integers $m$ and $n$
if and only if $N \in \{-2, -1, 0, 2\}$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 2.5 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-5`).

articles.title: $\bar P_n$ equals $F_{n-1}$ exactly for powers of two
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, let $\bar P_n$ be the
Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial, and let $F_{n-1} = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{n-1} \bar T_k$ be the partial
sum of the monic Chebyshev polynomials. Then $\bar P_n = F_{n-1}$ if and only if $n = 2^k$ for
some natural number $k$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Corollary 4.5 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-cor-17`).

articles.title: Odd-divisor formula for the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$, and for each
odd divisor $d$ of $n$ put $r_n(d) = n/d - (d+1)/2$, an integer. Then the Kassel–Reutenauer
polynomial $\bar P_n$ satisfies

$$
\bar P_n(X) = \sum_{d \mid n,\ d \text{ odd},\ r_n(d) \ge 0} F_{r_n(d)}(X) -
\sum_{d \mid n,\ d \text{ odd},\ r_n(d) < 0} F_{-r_n(d)-1}(X),
$$

where $F_r(X) = 1 + \sum_{k=1}^{r} \bar T_k(X)$ is the partial sum of the monic Chebyshev
polynomials $\bar T_k$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Theorem 4.4 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-thm-16`).

articles.title: Positivity of the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomials at integers $N \ge 2$
articles.statement:
For every $n \ge 1$
and every integer $N \ge 2$, the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial $\bar P_n$ satisfies
$\bar P_n(N) > 0$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 2.1 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-1`).

articles.title: Increasing-sequence formula for the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $n \ge 1$ and
work in the ring $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$ of Laurent polynomials. For integers $a$ and $h$ let
$IS(a, h) = \{a+1, \dots, a+h\}$. For an odd divisor $d$ of $n$ put $r_n(d) = n/d - (d+1)/2$,
$A_d = IS(r_n(d), d)$ and $\check A_d = IS(-r_n(d) - 1, 2n/d)$. Then the Kassel–Reutenauer
polynomial $\bar P_n$ satisfies

$$
\bar P_n(q + q^{-1}) = \sum_{d \mid n,\ d \text{ odd},\ r_n(d) \ge 0}\
\sum_{i \in \check A_d \setminus A_d} q^i -
\sum_{d \mid n,\ d \text{ odd},\ r_n(d) < 0}\ \sum_{i \in A_d \setminus \check A_d} q^i.
$$

The left-hand side is the paper's $P_n(q)/q^{n-1}$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 6.2 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-27`).

articles.title: Almost multiplicativity at a primitive sixth root of unity
articles.statement:
Let $\omega \in \mathbb{C}$ be a
primitive sixth root of unity, and for $n \ge 1$ let $v_n = |\bar P_n(\omega + \omega^{-1})|$,
where $\bar P_n$ is the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial. Let $m, n \ge 1$ be coprime. Then
$v_m v_n = v_{mn}$ if $(m \bmod 3, n \bmod 3)$ is $(0, 1)$, $(1, 1)$ or $(1, 2)$;
$v_m v_n = 2 v_{mn}$ if $(m \bmod 3, n \bmod 3) = (0, 2)$; and $v_m v_n = 4 v_{mn}$ if
$(m \bmod 3, n \bmod 3) = (2, 2)$. The residue pairs are ordered: nothing is claimed for the
swapped pairs.

Since $|\omega| = 1$, $v_n$ is the absolute value $|P_n(\omega)|$ of the paper's polynomial
$P_n(q) = q^{n-1} \bar P_n(q + q^{-1})$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 2.3 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-3`).

articles.title: Multiplicativity at roots of unity of order at most 4
articles.statement:
Let $q \in \mathbb{C}$ be a primitive
$d$-th root of unity with $d \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$, and let $\bar P_n$ be the Kassel–Reutenauer
polynomials. Then for all coprime integers $m, n \ge 1$,

$$
|\bar P_{mn}(q + q^{-1})| = |\bar P_m(q + q^{-1})| \, |\bar P_n(q + q^{-1})|.
$$

Since $|q| = 1$, $|\bar P_n(q + q^{-1})|$ is the absolute value $|P_n(q)|$ of the paper's
polynomial $P_n(q) = q^{n-1} \bar P_n(q + q^{-1})$, so $n \mapsto |P_n(q)|$ is multiplicative.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Proposition 2.2 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-prop-2`).

articles.title: The first Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial
articles.statement:
The Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial $\bar P_1$ is the
constant polynomial $1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Table 2.

articles.title: Multiplicativity of $\bar P_n^2$ modulo $X (X + 1) (X^2 - 4)$
articles.statement:
Let $\bar P_n$ be the
Kassel–Reutenauer polynomials. For coprime integers $m, n \ge 1$, the polynomial
$\bar P_{mn}(X)^2 - \bar P_m(X)^2 \bar P_n(X)^2$ is divisible in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ by
$X (X + 1) (X^2 - 4)$; if moreover $(m \bmod 3, n \bmod 3)$ is $(0, 1)$, $(1, 1)$ or $(1, 2)$,
it is divisible by $X (X + 1) (X^2 - 4) (X - 1)$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Corollary 2.4 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-cor-4`).

articles.title: Approximation of $\bar P_n$ by $F_{n-1}$
articles.statement:
Let $\bar P_n$ be the Kassel–Reutenauer
polynomials, and for $r \ge 0$ let $F_r(X) = 1 + \sum_{j=1}^{r} \bar T_j(X)$ be the partial sum
of the monic Chebyshev polynomials $\bar T_j$. For $n \ge 2$, every nonzero coefficient of
$\bar P_n(X) - F_{n-1}(X)$ sits in a degree $k$ with $2k + 2 < n$; that is, the difference has
degree less than $n/2 - 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Theorem 4.1 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-thm-12`).

articles.title: The third Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial
articles.statement:
The Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial $\bar P_3$ is
$X^2 + X - 2$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Table 2.

articles.title: Top coefficients of the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomials
articles.statement:
For $n \ge 10$, the polynomial

$$
\bar P_n(X) - \Bigl(X^{n-1} + X^{n-2} - (n-2) X^{n-3} - (n-3) X^{n-4} +
\tbinom{n-3}{2} X^{n-5} + \tbinom{n-4}{2} X^{n-6}\Bigr)
$$

has degree less than $n - 6$, where $\bar P_n$ is the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial. That is, up
to terms of degree at most $n - 7$, $\bar P_n(X)$ equals
$X^{n-1} + X^{n-2} - (n-2) X^{n-3} - (n-3) X^{n-4} + \frac{(n-3)(n-4)}{2} X^{n-5} +
\frac{(n-4)(n-5)}{2} X^{n-6}$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Corollary 4.2 (`jis-2026-26.4.4-cor-13`).

articles.title: The Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial $\bar P_2$
articles.statement:
The Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial
$\bar P_2(X) \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ equals $X + 1$.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, Table 2.

articles.title: Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial
articles.statement:
For a natural number $n$, the Kassel–Reutenauer polynomial
$\bar P_n(X) \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is defined by

$$
\bar P_n(X) = a_{n,0} + \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} a_{n,i} \, \bar T_i(X),
$$

where $a_{n,i}$ is the number of divisors $d$ of $n$ with $d(d - 2i) \le 2n$ and
$n < 2d(d - i)$ (equivalently, $(i + \sqrt{2n + i^2})/2 < d \le i + \sqrt{2n + i^2}$), and
$\bar T_i$ is the monic Chebyshev polynomial: $\bar T_0 = 2$, $\bar T_1 = X$ and
$\bar T_{i+2} = X \bar T_{i+1} - \bar T_i$. For $n = 0$ the sum is empty and the set of divisors
of $0$ is taken to be empty, so $\bar P_0 = 0$.

In the paper, $\bar P_n$ is characterized for $n \ge 1$ by
$\bar P_n(q + q^{-1}) = P_n(q)/q^{n-1}$, where $(q - 1)^2 P_n(q)$ is the number of ideals of
codimension $n$ of $\mathbb{F}_q[x, y, x^{-1}, y^{-1}]$; the definition here uses the explicit
expansion (2.4) of the paper instead.

## Sources

- C. Kassel and C. Reutenauer, *Pairs of Intertwined Integer Sequences*, Journal of Integer Sequences 29 (2026), Article 26.4.4, (2.1)–(2.4) and Table 2.

articles.title: Moment generating function as a J-fraction
articles.statement:
Let $p_0, p_1, \dots$ be real polynomials, each
$p_n$ monic of degree $n$, let $L$ be an $\mathbb{R}$-linear functional on $\mathbb{R}[x]$, and
let $(\alpha_n)$, $(\beta_n)$ and $(\mu_k)$ be real sequences. Suppose that $p_0 = 1$,
$p_1 = x - \alpha_0$ and $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) p_n - \beta_n p_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 1$, that
$\beta_n \ne 0$ for $n \ge 1$, that the $p_n$ are orthogonal for $L$, meaning $L(p_m p_n) = 0$
for $m \ne n$ and $L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ for every $n$, that $\mu_k = L(x^k)$ for every $k$, and that
$\mu_0 \ne 0$. Let $g = \sum_{k \ge 0} \mu_k x^k$ be the moment generating function. Then there
are formal power series $S_0, S_1, \dots$ over $\mathbb{R}$, each with constant term $1$, such
that $g = \mu_0 S_0$ and $S_n (1 - \alpha_n x - \beta_{n+1} x^2 S_{n+1}) = 1$ for every
$n \ge 0$.

These equations present $g$ as the J-fraction
$\mu_0 / (1 - \alpha_0 x - \beta_1 x^2 / (1 - \alpha_1 x - \beta_2 x^2 / \cdots))$ with tails
$S_n$. The hypotheses that each $p_n$ is monic of degree $n$, that $\beta_n \ne 0$, that
$L(p_n^2) \ne 0$ and that $\mu_0 \ne 0$ are not needed, and orthogonality is used only through
$L(p_n) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$.

The source's recurrence line reads $\beta_n(x)$; it is read as $\beta_n p_{n-1}$, as in the
surrounding lines 315–317 and 364–366 of the source.

## Sources

- Paul Barry and Aoife Hennessy, "Meixner-Type Results for Riordan Arrays and Associated Integer Sequences," Journal of Integer Sequences 13 (2010), Article 10.9.4, J-fraction theorem citing C. Krattenthaler (cf. Viennot Proposition 1, (7), p. V-5; Wall Theorem 51.1), lines 353–362, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/Barry5/barry96s.tex

articles.title: Moment generating function as a J-fraction, general form
articles.statement:
Let $p_0, p_1, \dots$ be real
polynomials, let $L$ be an $\mathbb{R}$-linear functional on $\mathbb{R}[x]$, and let
$(\alpha_n)$, $(\beta_n)$ and $(\mu_k)$ be real sequences such that $p_0 = 1$,
$p_1 = x - \alpha_0$, $p_{n+1} = (x - \alpha_n) p_n - \beta_n p_{n-1}$ for $n \ge 1$,
$\mu_k = L(x^k)$ for every $k$, and $L(p_n) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$. Then there are formal power
series $S_0, S_1, \dots$ over $\mathbb{R}$, each with constant term $1$, giving $\mu$ a Jacobi
fraction with coefficients $\alpha$ and $\beta$, numerator $\mu_0$ and tails $S_n$: that is,
$\sum_{k \ge 0} \mu_k x^k = \mu_0 S_0$ and $(1 - \alpha_n x - \beta_{n+1} x^2 S_{n+1}) S_n = 1$
for every $n \ge 0$.

No monicity, degree or $\beta_n \ne 0$ hypothesis is needed, and orthogonality enters only
through $L(p_n) = 0$ for $n \ge 1$.

articles.title: Meixner-type characterization of Riordan orthogonal polynomial arrays
articles.statement:
Let $d$ and $h$ be
real formal power series with $[x^0]\,h = 0$, $[x^1]\,h \ne 0$ and $[x^0]\,d \ne 0$, where
$[x^n]$ denotes the coefficient of $x^n$, and let $L$ be the Riordan array of $(d, h)$, with
entries $L_{n,k} = [x^n]\,(d h^k)$ for $n, k \ge 0$. Call $L$ a monic orthogonal coefficient
array if there are real polynomials $P_0, P_1, \dots$ with $[x^k]\,P_n = L_{n,k}$ for all
$n, k$, each $P_n$ monic, and the family $(P_n)$ formally orthogonal. Each of the following
three conditions is equivalent to $L$ being a monic orthogonal coefficient array.

1. Meixner form: there are real numbers $\lambda, \mu, r, s$ with $s \ne 0$ and $s + \mu \ne 0$
   such that $d\,(1 + r x + s x^2) = 1 - \lambda x - \mu x^2$ and $h\,(1 + r x + s x^2) = x$.
2. Stieltjes form of the inverse: $L_{0,0} = 1$, and there are an array $(L'_{n,k})$ and real
   numbers $r_1, s_1, r, s$ with $s_1 \ne 0$ and $s \ne 0$ such that $L_{n,k} = L'_{n,k} = 0$
   whenever $k > n$; $\sum_{j=0}^{n} L_{n,j} L'_{j,k}$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n} L'_{n,j} L_{j,k}$
   both equal $1$ if $n = k$ and $0$ otherwise; and
   $L'_{n+1,k} = \sum_{j=0}^{n+1} L'_{n,j} S_{j,k}$ for all $n, k$, where $S$ is the
   Stieltjes matrix with parameters $r_1, s_1, r, s$: its superdiagonal entries are $1$, its
   diagonal is $r_1, r, r, \dots$, its subdiagonal is $s_1, s, s, \dots$, and all other
   entries are $0$.
3. Coefficient recurrence: there are real numbers $\lambda, \mu, r, s$ with $s \ne 0$ and
   $s + \mu \ne 0$ such that for all $N, K \ge 0$,
   $L_{N,K} + r L_{N-1,K} - L_{N-1,K-1} + s L_{N-2,K} = c_{N,K}$, where any entry of $L$
   with a negative index is read as $0$, $c_{0,0} = 1$, $c_{1,0} = -\lambda$,
   $c_{2,0} = -\mu$, and $c_{N,K} = 0$ otherwise.

Proof: The coefficient recurrence is the common hub. The Meixner equivalence follows from
Barry-Hennessy, the orthogonality equivalence from Favard's theorem as in Chihara, and the
inverse-array equivalence from the Stieltjes production construction of the inverse array.

## Sources

- Paul Barry and Aoife Hennessy, "Meixner-Type Results for Riordan Arrays and Associated Integer Sequences," Journal of Integer Sequences 13 (2010), Article 10.9.4, Proposition (referee's summary of the main results), lines 733–752, https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL13/Barry5/barry96s.tex

articles.title: The factor $(x - 1)^n$ for polynomials with distinct real roots
articles.statement:
Let $c$ be a real
number, let $s$ be a finite set of real numbers, and let $f(x) = c \prod_{r \in s} (x - r)$ in
$\mathbb{R}[x]$. For every natural number $n$, the polynomial $(x - 1)^n$ divides the polynomial

$$\sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} \prod_{0 \le k \le n,\ k \ne i} f(x^k).$$

For $c \ne 0$ and $1 \notin s$ (the paper's conditions), this polynomial is the numerator of
$Q_n(x; f) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} / f(x^i)$ over the common denominator
$\prod_{k=0}^{n} f(x^k)$; for $c = 0$ or $1 \in s$ some $f(x^k)$ is zero and only the
polynomial statement remains.

## Sources

- Takashi Agoh, *An Intrinsic Factor of an Alternating Sum Involving Certain Rational Functions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A9, Theorem 3.1.

articles.title: The factor $(x - 1)^n$ of an alternating binomial sum
articles.statement:
For every real number $a$ and
every natural number $n$, the polynomial $(x - 1)^n$ divides, in $\mathbb{R}[x]$, the polynomial

$$H_n(x; a) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} \prod_{0 \le k \le n,\ k \ne i} (x^k + a).$$

For $a \ne -1$ (the paper's condition), $H_n(x; a)$ is the numerator of
$G_n(x; a) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} (-1)^i \binom{n}{i} / (x^i + a)$ over the common denominator
$\prod_{k=0}^{n} (x^k + a)$; at $a = -1$ the factor $x^0 + a$ is zero and only the polynomial
statement remains.

## Sources

- Takashi Agoh, *An Intrinsic Factor of an Alternating Sum Involving Certain Rational Functions*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A9, Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Binomial products of series with a cubic denominator
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic
$0$, let $A, B, C \in K$ with $C \ne 0$, and let $D(x) = 1 + Ax + Bx^2 + Cx^3$. Suppose that
$D(x) = \prod_{i=1}^{3} (1 - \alpha_i x)$ with $\alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3 \in K$ and that
$2\alpha_i \ne \alpha_j + \alpha_k$ whenever $i, j, k \in \{1, 2, 3\}$ are not all equal. Let $r$
and $s$ be power series over $K$ such that $r D$ and $s D$ are polynomials of degree less than $3$.
Then there are polynomials $u$, $v$ over $K$ of degree at most $2$ such that

$$r \odot s = \frac{u(x)}{D(2x)} + \frac{1}{1 + Ax} \odot \frac{v(x)}{D(-x)},$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product.

The second term uses the factor $1/(1 + Ax)$; with $1/(1 - Ax)$ in its place the statement already
fails for the tribonacci series $x/(1 - x - x^2 - x^3)$, where $A = -1$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 12 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-12`).

articles.title: Binomial product with a geometric series
articles.statement:
For every field $K$ of characteristic $0$, every
power series $A(x)$ over $K$ and every $\beta \in K$,

$$A(x) \odot \frac{1}{1 - \beta x} = \frac{1}{1 - \beta x} A\left(\frac{x}{1 - \beta x}\right),$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product and $A(x/(1 - \beta x))$ is the substitution of the series
$x/(1 - \beta x)$, which has zero constant term, into $A$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Corollary 5 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-cor-5`).

articles.title: Binomial square of the Lucas generating function
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic
$0$, let $a, b \in K$, and let $g(x) = \sum_{n \ge 0} G_n x^n$ be a power series over $K$ with
$g(x)(1 - ax - bx^2) = 2 - ax$. Then

$$g \odot g = \frac{2}{1 - ax} + g(2x),$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product, and
$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} G_k G_{n-k} = 2a^n + 2^n G_n$ for every $n \ge 0$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 11 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-11`).

articles.title: Binomial products of arbitrary rational series
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$,
let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n$ be nonzero elements of $K$, and let
$R$, $S$ be polynomials over $K$. Let $A$, $B$ be power series over $K$ with
$A(x) \prod_{i=1}^m (1 - \alpha_i x) = R(x)$ and $B(x) \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - \beta_j x) = S(x)$.
Put $u = \max(d_R + 1 - m, 0)$ and $v = \max(d_S + 1 - n, 0)$, where $d_R$ and $d_S$ are the
degrees of $R$ and $S$, the zero polynomial counting as degree $0$. Then there is a polynomial
$T$ over $K$ of degree less than $(u + m)(v + n)$ such that

$$(A \odot B)(x) \Big(\prod_{i=1}^m (1 - \alpha_i x)\Big)^{v}
\Big(\prod_{j=1}^n (1 - \beta_j x)\Big)^{u} \prod_{i=1}^m \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - (\alpha_i + \beta_j) x)
= T(x),$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Corollary 7 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-cor-7`).

articles.title: Binomial products of proper rational series
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let
