$\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m, \beta_1, \dots, \beta_n \in K$, not necessarily distinct or nonzero,
and let $R$, $S$ be polynomials over $K$ with $\deg R < m$ and $\deg S < n$. If $A$, $B$ are power
series over $K$ with $A(x) \prod_{i=1}^m (1 - \alpha_i x) = R(x)$ and
$B(x) \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - \beta_j x) = S(x)$, then there is a polynomial $T$ over $K$ with
$\deg T < mn$ such that

$$(A \odot B)(x) \prod_{i=1}^m \prod_{j=1}^n \bigl(1 - (\alpha_i + \beta_j) x\bigr) = T(x),$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product.

Here $\deg 0 = -\infty$, so $T = 0$ when $mn = 0$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 6 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-6`).

articles.title: Binomial product of shifted powers of geometric series
articles.statement:
For every field $K$ of
characteristic $0$, all $j, k \in \mathbb{N}$ and all $\alpha, \beta \in K$,

$$\frac{x^j}{(1 - \alpha x)^{j+1}} \odot \frac{x^k}{(1 - \beta x)^{k+1}} =
\binom{j + k}{j} \frac{x^{j+k}}{(1 - (\alpha + \beta) x)^{j+k+1}},$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Lemma 4 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-lem-4`).

articles.title: Binomial product with a monomial
articles.statement:
For every field $K$ of characteristic $0$, every
$m \in \mathbb{N}$ and every power series $A(x)$ over $K$,

$$x^m \odot A(x) = \frac{x^m}{m!} \frac{d^m}{dx^m}\bigl(x^m A(x)\bigr),$$

where $\odot$ is the binomial product and $d/dx$ is the formal derivative.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Lemma 8 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-lem-8`).

articles.title: Binomial (Hurwitz) product of power series
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring. The binomial
product of formal power series $A = \sum_n a_n X^n$ and $B = \sum_n b_n X^n$ in $K[[X]]$ is the
power series $\sum_n c_n X^n$ with $c_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_k b_{n-k}$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, equation (1).

articles.title: Coefficients of the binomial product
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring and let
$A = \sum_n a_n X^n$ and $B = \sum_n b_n X^n$ be formal power series over $K$. For every natural
number $n$, the coefficient of $X^n$ in the binomial product of $A$ and $B$ is
$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} a_k b_{n-k}$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, equation (1).

articles.title: Constant coefficient of the binomial product
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a commutative ring. For formal
power series $A$ and $B$ over $K$, the constant coefficient of the binomial product of $A$ and
$B$ is the product of the constant coefficients of $A$ and $B$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, equation (1).

articles.title: Orthogonal vectors descend from field extensions
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $G$ be a field
extension of $F$ (a field with an $F$-algebra structure), let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let
$S \subseteq F^n$. If some nonzero $t \in G^n$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n s_i t_i = 0$ in $G$ for
every $s \in S$, then some nonzero $u \in F^n$ satisfies $\sum_{i=1}^n s_i u_i = 0$ for every
$s \in S$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Lemma 3 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-lem-3`).

articles.title: Rationality of power series descends from field extensions
articles.statement:
Let $F$ be a field, let $G$ be
a field extension of $F$ (a field with an $F$-algebra structure), and let $A$ be a power series
over $F$. If there are polynomials $p$, $q$ over $G$ with $q \ne 0$ and $A q = p$, where $A$ is
viewed as a power series over $G$, then there are polynomials $P$, $Q$ over $F$ with $Q \ne 0$ and
$A Q = P$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 1 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-1`).

articles.title: Hadamard products of rational series
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let
$\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m, \beta_1, \dots, \beta_n \in K$, and let $A = \sum_k a_k x^k$ and
$B = \sum_k b_k x^k$ be power series over $K$ such that $A(x) \prod_{i=1}^m (1 - \alpha_i x)$ and
$B(x) \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - \beta_j x)$ are polynomials. Then their Hadamard product
$A * B = \sum_k a_k b_k x^k$ has the property that
$(A * B)(x) \prod_{i=1}^m \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - \alpha_i \beta_j x)$ is a polynomial. Moreover, call a
power series $f$ over $K$ proper if $f Q = P$ for some polynomials $P$, $Q$ over $K$ with
$Q(0) \ne 0$ and $\deg P < \deg Q$. If $A$ and $B$ are proper, then so is $A * B$.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 13 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-13`).

articles.title: Resultant identity for pairwise sums
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let
$m, n \ge 0$ be integers, and let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n$ be
elements of $K$. Regard $f(y) = \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 - y - \alpha_i x)$ and
$g(y) = \prod_{j=1}^{n} (y - \beta_j x)$ as polynomials in $y$ with coefficients in $K[x]$,
and let $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(f, g)$ be the determinant of their Sylvester matrix formed with
the formal degrees $m$ and $n$. Then in $K[x]$

$$
\prod_{i=1}^{m} \prod_{j=1}^{n} \bigl(1 - (\alpha_i + \beta_j)x\bigr)
= (-1)^{mn} \operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(f, g).
$$

With $U(x) = \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 - \alpha_i x)$ and $V(x) = \prod_{j=1}^{n} (1 - \beta_j x)$, these
are $f(y) = (1 - y)^m U(x / (1 - y))$ and $g(y) = y^n V(x / y)$, the form used in the source.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 10 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-10`).

articles.title: Resultant identity for pairwise products
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, let
$m, n \ge 0$ be integers, and let $\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_m$ and $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_n$ be
elements of $K$. Regard $f(y) = \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 - \alpha_i y)$ and
$g(y) = \prod_{j=1}^{n} (y - \beta_j x)$ as polynomials in $y$ with coefficients in $K[x]$,
and let $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(f, g)$ be the determinant of their Sylvester matrix formed with
the formal degrees $m$ and $n$. Then in $K[x]$

$$
\prod_{i=1}^{m} \prod_{j=1}^{n} (1 - \alpha_i \beta_j x) = (-1)^{mn} \operatorname{Res}_{m,n}(f, g).
$$

With $U(x) = \prod_{i=1}^{m} (1 - \alpha_i x)$ and $V(x) = \prod_{j=1}^{n} (1 - \beta_j x)$, these
are $f(y) = U(y)$ and $g(y) = y^n V(x / y)$, the form used in the source.

## Sources

- Ira M. Gessel and Ishan Kar, *Binomial Convolutions for Rational Power Series*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.1.3, Theorem 14 (`jis-2024-24.1.3-thm-14`).

articles.title: Triangle inequality for the coefficient L1 norm
articles.statement: Adding polynomials increases the coefficient L1 norm by at most the sum.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm as a sum over a larger index set
articles.statement: Enlarging the summation set beyond the support does not change the sum.

articles.title: Upper bound on the coefficient L1 norm of a monomial
articles.statement: The coefficient L1 norm of a monomial is at most its absolute coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm of a monomial
articles.statement:
A monomial's coefficient L1 norm is the absolute value of its coefficient,
including when the coefficient is zero.

articles.title: Submultiplicativity of the coefficient L1 norm
articles.statement:
The coefficient convolution in a product is bounded by the product of the
coefficient L1 norms; cancellation can make this inequality strict.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the coefficient L1 norm
articles.statement: The coefficient L1 norm is nonnegative.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm of a scalar multiple
articles.statement: Rational scalar multiplication scales the norm by the scalar's absolute value.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm of a finite sum
articles.statement: The norm of a finite sum is bounded by the sum of the coefficient norms.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm of the zero polynomial
articles.statement: The zero polynomial has coefficient L1 norm zero.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm of a multivariate polynomial
articles.statement: The rational sum of the absolute values of a polynomial's coefficients.

articles.title: Coefficient L1 norm as an $\ell^1$ distance
articles.statement:
The real cast of the coefficient L1 norm agrees with the explicit exponent-one
metric on the exact rational coefficient Finsupp carrier.

articles.title: Binomial bound on coefficients of a product of affine polynomials
articles.statement:
If every constant and linear coefficient is at most one in absolute value,
then the absolute value of coefficient `i` is at most `S.card.choose i`.

articles.title: Coefficients of a product with a homogeneous linear polynomial
articles.statement:
The coefficient of `p * q`, when `p` is homogeneous of degree one, is the
sum obtained by removing one occurrence of each variable in the monomial.

articles.title: Coefficient recurrence for multiplication by a linear polynomial
articles.statement:
The coefficient at every index, including beyond the dense output, follows the source
recurrence `r * l[j] + c * l[j - 1]`.

articles.title: Length of the coefficient list after a linear multiplication
articles.statement: A linear-coefficient update always adds one dense coefficient.

articles.title: Coefficient list after multiplication by a linear polynomial
articles.statement: The dense little-endian coefficients after left multiplication by `C r + X * C c`.

articles.title: Coefficient-list multiplication agrees with polynomial multiplication
articles.statement:
Interpreting the dense output as a little-endian polynomial is left multiplication by the
linear polynomial `C r + X * C c`.

articles.title: Coefficients of a product of affine linear polynomials
articles.statement:
The coefficient of degree `i` in a product of affine linear polynomials is
the sum over the `i` factors from which the linear term is selected.

articles.title: Expansion of a product of affine linear polynomials
articles.statement:
Expand a product of affine linear polynomials by the subset of factors
from which the linear term is selected.

articles.title: Degree bound for a product of affine linear polynomials
articles.statement:
A product of affine linear polynomials has degree at most the number of
factors.

articles.title: The Artin–Hasse exponential has $p$-integral coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let
$F(z) = \exp\big(\sum_{j \ge 0} z^{p^j} / p^j\big) \in \mathbb{Q}[[z]]$ be the Artin–Hasse
exponential. For every $n \ge 0$, the coefficient of $z^n$ in $F$, written in lowest terms, has a
denominator not divisible by $p$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 29.

articles.title: The Artin–Hasse exponential as a product
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $\mu$ be the Möbius
function and let $F(z) = \exp\big(\sum_{j \ge 0} z^{p^j} / p^j\big) \in \mathbb{Q}[[z]]$ be the
Artin–Hasse exponential. For $d \ge 1$ and $a \in \mathbb{Q}$ write
$(1 - z^d)^a = \exp\big(a \log(1 - z^d)\big)$, where $\log(1 - z^d) = -\sum_{k \ge 1} z^{dk}/k$.
Then for every $N \ge 0$, $F$ has the same coefficients of $z^0, \dots, z^N$ as the finite product
of the series $(1 - z^d)^{-\mu(d)/d}$ over the integers $1 \le d \le N$ not divisible by $p$.
Since the factors with $d > N$ are $1 + O(z^{N+1})$, this is the identity
$F(z) = \prod_{p \nmid d} (1 - z^d)^{-\mu(d)/d}$ read coefficientwise.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 27.

articles.title: Elementary symmetric polynomials in terms of power sums
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a finite set of
variables, and in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ let $e_n$ be the $n$-th elementary symmetric
polynomial and $p_k = \sum_{i \in \sigma} x_i^k$ the $k$-th power sum. For a partition $\lambda$
of $n$ with parts $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\ell$, write
$p_\lambda = p_{\lambda_1} \cdots p_{\lambda_\ell}$, $\varepsilon_\lambda = (-1)^{n - \ell}$ and
$z_\lambda = \prod_a a^{r_a} \, r_a!$, where $r_a$ is the number of parts equal to $a$ and the
product runs over the distinct parts $a$. Then for every $n \ge 0$,

$$e_n = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} \frac{\varepsilon_\lambda}{z_\lambda} \, p_\lambda.$$

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 21.

articles.title: The generating function of the elementary symmetric polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a finite
set of variables, and in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ let $e_k$ be the $k$-th elementary
symmetric polynomial and $p_n = \sum_{i \in \sigma} x_i^n$ the $n$-th power sum. Then, as formal
power series in $t$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$,

$$\sum_{k \ge 0} e_k t^k = \exp\Big(\sum_{n \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n} p_n t^n\Big).$$

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 20.

articles.title: Exponential of a power-sum series restricted to a set of degrees
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a finite
set of variables, and in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ let $p_s = \sum_{i \in \sigma} x_i^s$
be the $s$-th power sum. Let $S$ be a set of natural numbers and let
$P_S(t) = \sum_{s \in S,\ s \ge 1} \frac{(-1)^{s-1}}{s} p_s t^s$. For a partition $\lambda$ of
$n$ with parts $\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_\ell$, write
$p_\lambda = p_{\lambda_1} \cdots p_{\lambda_\ell}$, $\varepsilon_\lambda = (-1)^{n - \ell}$ and
$z_\lambda = \prod_a a^{r_a} \, r_a!$, where $r_a$ is the number of parts equal to $a$ and the
product runs over the distinct parts $a$. Then, as formal power series in $t$ with coefficients
in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$, $\exp P_S(t) = \sum_{n \ge 0} c_n t^n$, where $c_n$ is the
sum of $\varepsilon_\lambda p_\lambda / z_\lambda$ over the partitions $\lambda$ of $n$ all of
whose parts lie in $S$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 19.

articles.title: Ideals with divided powers are divided-power ideals
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be an ideal of a commutative
ring $A$. If $I$ carries a divided-power structure $(\gamma_k)_{k \ge 0}$ in the usual sense, then
$I$ is a divided-power ideal: for every $a \in I$ and every $k \ge 1$ there is $c \in I$ with
$a^k = k!\, c$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 2.2 (the maps `γ_k(a) = a ^ k / k!`).

articles.title: The zero ideal is a divided-power ideal
articles.statement:
In every commutative ring, the zero ideal is a
divided-power ideal.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 2.2 (the definition).

articles.title: The $p$-th power criterion for divided-power ideals
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $A$ be a
commutative ring in which every natural number not divisible by $p$ is a unit (a
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra). An ideal $\mathfrak{a}$ of $A$ is a divided-power ideal if and only if
for every $a \in \mathfrak{a}$ there is $c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $a^p = p\,c$, that is,
$a^p \in p\mathfrak{a}$.

The paper also assumes $A$ torsion-free; the statement does not need it.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 4.

articles.title: When the maximal ideal of a DVR is a divided-power ideal
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let $O$ be
a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ such that $pO = \mathfrak{m}^e$ for
some integer $e \ge 1$. Then $\mathfrak{m}$ is a divided-power ideal if and only if $e \le p - 1$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 8.

articles.title: Powers of the maximal ideal of a DVR that are divided-power ideals
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and
let $O$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak{m}$ such that
$pO = \mathfrak{m}^e$ for some integer $e \ge 1$. Then for every $k \ge 0$, the ideal
$\mathfrak{m}^k$ is a divided-power ideal if and only if $e \le (p - 1)k$.

Equivalently, with $v_p(\mathfrak{m}) = 1/e$, the condition is $v_p(\mathfrak{m}^k) \ge 1/(p - 1)$.
The paper states this for $p$-adic discrete valuation rings and remarks that it also holds for
localizations of rings of integers; here $O$ is any such ring, and the zero ideal is omitted.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Lemma 7.

articles.title: Divided-power ideals generated by a set
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $A$ a commutative ring in
which every natural number not divisible by $p$ is a unit (a $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra). For a
subset $S \subseteq A$, the ideal $\mathfrak{a}$ generated by $S$ is a divided-power ideal if and
only if for every $a \in S$ there is $c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $a^p = pc$, that is,
$a^p \in p\mathfrak{a}$.

Torsion-freeness of $A$ is not needed.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 5.

articles.title: $(p)$ is a divided-power ideal of $\mathbb{Z}_p$
articles.statement:
For every prime $p$, the ideal generated
by $p$ in the ring $\mathbb{Z}_p$ of $p$-adic integers is a divided-power ideal.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 8, last sentence.

articles.title: Divided-power ideal
articles.statement:
An ideal $I$ of a commutative ring $A$ is a *divided-power ideal* when
for every $a \in I$ and every integer $k \ge 1$ there is $c \in I$ with $a^k = k! \, c$, that is,
$a^k \in k! \, I$. For a prime $p$, in a torsion-free $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra this says
$a^k / k! \in I$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 2.2.

articles.title: $p$ copies of $u$ form a $p$-splitting of $\{pu\}$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $p$ and every
integer $u \ge 1$, the multiset consisting of $p$ copies of $u$ is a $p$-splitting of the
one-element multiset $\{pu\}$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Definition 30.

articles.title: $p$-splitting of multisets of parts
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a natural number and $s$, $t$ multisets of
natural numbers (multisets of parts). Then $s$ is a *$p$-splitting* of $t$ when there is $u \ge 1$
such that $t$ contains the part $pu$ and $s$ is obtained from $t$ by removing one instance of $pu$
and adding $p$ copies of $u$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Definition 30.

articles.title: Product of a divided-power ideal with an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring. If
$\mathfrak{a}$ is a divided-power ideal of $A$, then for every ideal $\mathfrak{b}$ of $A$ the
product $\mathfrak{a}\mathfrak{b}$ is a divided-power ideal.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 6.

articles.title: Congruence of products over a partition with multiplicities divisible by $p^v$
articles.statement:
Let $p$
be a prime, $A$ a commutative ring and $\mathfrak{a}$ a divided-power ideal of $A$. Let
$f, g : \mathbb{N} \to A$ satisfy $f_n - g_n \in \mathfrak{a}$ for every $n \ge 1$. For a
partition $\lambda = (\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_k)$ of a natural number $m$, write
$f_\lambda = f_{\lambda_1} \cdots f_{\lambda_k}$ and
$g_\lambda = g_{\lambda_1} \cdots g_{\lambda_k}$. If $v$ is a natural number such that every part
of $\lambda$ occurs a multiple of $p^v$ times, then $f_\lambda - g_\lambda = p^v c$ for some
$c \in \mathfrak{a}$, that is, $f_\lambda \equiv g_\lambda \bmod p^v \mathfrak{a}$.

The paper takes $v = v_p(\lambda) = \min_i v_p(\lambda_i)$, which is false: for $p = 2$,
$\lambda = (2)$, $A = \mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$, $\mathfrak{a} = (2)$, $f_n = e_n(X^2 + 2)$ and
$g_n = e_n(X^2)$, where $e_n(P)$ is the $n$-th elementary symmetric function of the roots of $P$,
$f_n \equiv g_n \bmod 2$ for all $n$ but $f_2 - g_2 = 2 \notin 4\mathbb{Z}_{(2)}$. The paper's
proof writes $\lambda = \mu^{p^v}$ in the partition monoid, which uses the multiplicity condition
stated here. The paper's symmetric functions are abstracted to arbitrary sequences $f, g$, as the
statement only uses their values.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 26.

articles.title: Multiplicativity of $g_\lambda$ over disjoint parts
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $\sigma$ a finite
set of variables, and for a multiset $\lambda$ of parts let $g_\lambda$ be its $p$-equivalence class
sum in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$. Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be multisets of natural numbers,
none of whose elements is divisible by $p$ (so no part is $0$), with no part in common. Then
$g_{\lambda + \mu} = g_\lambda \, g_\mu$, where $\lambda + \mu$ is the union of $\lambda$ and $\mu$
counted with multiplicity. Moreover $g_\lambda = \prod_u g_{(u)^{r_u(\lambda)}}$, the product over
the distinct parts $u$ of $\lambda$, where $r_u(\lambda)$ is the number of times $u$ occurs in
$\lambda$ and $(u)^r$ is the multiset of $r$ copies of $u$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Lemma 34.

articles.title: $g_\lambda$ is $p$-integral
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $\sigma$ a finite set of variables and
$\lambda$ a partition of $n$. Every coefficient of the $p$-equivalence class sum $g_\lambda$ in
$\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ is a rational number whose denominator in lowest terms is not
divisible by $p$.

This is the paper's $g_\lambda \in \Lambda_{\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}}$, in finitely many variables.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 36.

articles.title: For odd $p$ the signs in $g_\lambda$ are constant
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be an odd prime, $\sigma$ a
finite set of variables and $\lambda$ a partition of $n$ with $\ell(\lambda)$ parts. Then the
$p$-equivalence class sum $g_\lambda$ in $\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ satisfies

$$g_\lambda = (-1)^{n - \ell(\lambda)} \sum_{\mu \in C_\lambda} \frac{p_\mu}{z_\mu},$$

where $C_\lambda$ is the $p$-equivalence class of $\lambda$ (the partitions $\mu$ of $n$ with
$\mu \sim_p \lambda$), $p_\mu = \prod_i p_{\mu_i}$ is the product of the power sums
$p_k = \sum_{i \in \sigma} x_i^k$, and $z_\mu = \prod_a a^{r_a} \, r_a!$, the product over the
distinct parts $a$ of $\mu$, with $r_a$ the number of parts of $\mu$ equal to $a$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Lemma 35.

articles.title: The class sum of the empty partition
articles.statement:
For every finite set of variables $\sigma$ and every
natural number $p$, the $p$-equivalence class sum of the empty multiset is $g_\emptyset = 1$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 5.2.

articles.title: The $p$-equivalence class sum
articles.statement:
Let $\sigma$ be a finite set of variables, let $p$ be a
natural number and let $\lambda$ be a multiset of natural numbers whose elements sum to $n$. In
$\mathbb{Q}[x_i : i \in \sigma]$ let $p_k = \sum_{i \in \sigma} x_i^k$ be the $k$-th power sum. For
a partition $\mu$ of $n$ with parts $\mu_1, \dots, \mu_\ell$, write
$p_\mu = p_{\mu_1} \cdots p_{\mu_\ell}$, $\varepsilon_\mu = (-1)^{n - \ell}$ and
$z_\mu = \prod_a a^{r_a} \, r_a!$, where $r_a$ is the number of parts of $\mu$ equal to $a$ and the
product runs over the distinct parts $a$ of $\mu$. The $p$-equivalence class sum of $\lambda$ is

$$g_\lambda = \sum_{\mu \in C_\lambda} \frac{\varepsilon_\mu}{z_\mu} \, p_\mu,$$

where $C_\lambda$ is the $p$-equivalence class of $\lambda$: the set of partitions of $n$ that are
$p$-equivalent to $\lambda$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 5.2, display (8).

articles.title: The $p$-equivalence class of a multiset of parts
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a natural number and $\lambda$
a multiset of natural numbers whose elements sum to $n$. The $p$-equivalence class $C_\lambda$ is
the set of partitions $\mu$ of $n$ with $\mu \sim_p \lambda$, where $\sim_p$ ($p$-equivalence) is
the equivalence relation on multisets of natural numbers generated by $p$-splitting.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Definition 31.

articles.title: Kummer's theorem for multinomial coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and let
$r_1, \dots, r_k$ be natural numbers with sum $m$. For $i \ge 1$ let
$c_i = \lfloor ((r_1 \bmod p^i) + \dots + (r_k \bmod p^i)) / p^i \rfloor$. Then

$$v_p\binom{m}{r_1, \dots, r_k} = \sum_{i=1}^{m} c_i.$$

Here $c_i$ is the carry into digit position $i$ when $r_1 + \dots + r_k$ is added in base $p$, and
$c_i = 0$ for $i > m$, so the right side is the sum of all the carries.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Theorem 23.

articles.title: A valuation bound from Kummer's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $r_1, \dots, r_k$ be
natural numbers with sum $m$, and let $j$ be an index with $r_j \ne 0$. Then

$$v_p(m) \le v_p(r_j) + v_p\binom{m}{r_1, \dots, r_k},$$

that is, $v_p(r_j) \ge v_p(m) - v_p\binom{m}{r_1, \dots, r_k}$.

The hypothesis $r_j \ne 0$ is needed because $v_p(0)$ is taken to be $0$: for $(r_1, r_2) = (0, p)$
the inequality fails at $j = 1$. With the paper's convention $v_p(0) = \infty$ that case is trivial.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Corollary 24.

articles.title: Elementary symmetric functions vanish above the degree
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a polynomial of degree
$d$ over a commutative ring, with $d = 0$ for $P = 0$. Then $e_n(P) = 0$ for every $n > d$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2, Notation.

articles.title: Power-sum congruences imply elementary symmetric congruences
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and $A$ a
torsion-free commutative ring in which every natural number not divisible by $p$ is a unit (a
torsion-free $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra). Let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a divided-power ideal of $A$, let
$P, Q \in A[X]$ be monic and let $N$ be a natural number. Suppose that for every $n$ with
$1 \le n \le N$ there is $c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $p_n(P) - p_n(Q) = n c$, that is,
$p_n(P) \equiv p_n(Q) \pmod{n \mathfrak{a}}$. Then $e_n(P) - e_n(Q) \in \mathfrak{a}$ for every $n$
with $1 \le n \le N$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 13.

articles.title: The zeroth elementary symmetric function of a monic polynomial
articles.statement:
For every monic
polynomial $P$ over a commutative ring, $e_0(P) = 1$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2, Notation.

articles.title: Elementary symmetric functions of a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $P$ be a polynomial of degree $d$ over
a commutative ring, with $d = 0$ for $P = 0$. For a natural number $n$, $e_n(P)$ is $(-1)^n$ times
the coefficient of $X^{d - n}$ in $P$ if $n \le d$, and $0$ if $n > d$. In particular
$e_0(P) = 1$ when $P$ is monic.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2, Notation.

articles.title: The first power sum is the first elementary symmetric function
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $P$
over a commutative ring, $p_1(P) = e_1(P)$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2 (Newton's identities).

articles.title: Congruent elementary symmetric functions give deep power-sum congruences
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
prime and let $A$ be a commutative ring without additive torsion in which every natural number
not divisible by $p$ is a unit (a torsion-free $\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra). Let
$\mathfrak{a}$ be a divided-power ideal of $A$, let $P, Q \in A[X]$ be monic and let $N \ge 1$;
write $e_n$ and $p_n$ for the elementary symmetric functions and power sums of a polynomial.
If $e_n(P) - e_n(Q) \in \mathfrak{a}$ for every $n$ with $1 \le n \le N$, then there is
$c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $p_N(P) - p_N(Q) = N c$, that is,
$p_N(P) \equiv p_N(Q) \pmod{N \mathfrak{a}}$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 12.

articles.title: Newton's recurrence for the power sums of a polynomial
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $P$ over a
commutative ring and every $n \ge 0$, writing $e_i = e_i(P)$ and $p_i = p_i(P)$ for the
elementary symmetric functions and power sums of $P$,

$$p_{n+1} = (-1)^n (n+1)\, e_{n+1} + \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} (-1)^i e_{i+1}\, p_{n-i}.$$

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2 (Newton's identities).

articles.title: The zeroth power sum of a polynomial is its degree
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $P$ over a
commutative ring $A$, the power sum $p_0(P)$ equals the degree of $P$ as a natural number
(taken to be $0$ for $P = 0$), viewed as an element of $A$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Section 3.2, Notation.

articles.title: Power sums of a polynomial
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $P$ over a commutative ring $A$, with
elementary symmetric functions $e_i = e_i(P)$, the power sums $p_n = p_n(P) \in A$ are defined
recursively: $p_0$ is the degree of $P$ as a natural number ($0$ for $P = 0$), and for
$n \ge 1$ Newton's identity holds:

$$p_n = \sum_{i=1}^{n-1} (-1)^{i-1} e_i\, p_{n-i} + (-1)^{n-1} n\, e_n.$$

If $P$ is monic and $P = (X - \alpha_1) \cdots (X - \alpha_d)$, then
$p_n = \alpha_1^n + \cdots + \alpha_d^n$ for every $n$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Sections 2.1 and 3.2 (Newton's identities, Macdonald I.2.11').

articles.title: A prime-exponent criterion for powers in an ideal
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $v_p$ the $p$-adic
valuation, and $\mathfrak{b}$ an ideal of a commutative ring $B$.
The following are equivalent: for every $n \ge 1$ and every $a \in \mathfrak{b}$ there is
$c \in \mathfrak{b}$ with $a^n = p^{v_p(n!)} c$; and for every $a \in \mathfrak{b}$ there is
$c \in \mathfrak{b}$ with $a^p = p c$.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Proposition 3.

articles.title: Powers of elements congruent modulo a divided-power ideal
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, let $A$ be
a commutative ring in which every natural number not divisible by $p$ is a unit (a
$\mathbb{Z}_{(p)}$-algebra), and let $\mathfrak{a}$ be a divided-power ideal of $A$. If
$x, y \in A$ satisfy $x - y \in \mathfrak{a}$, then for every $m \ge 0$ there is
$c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $x^{p^m} - y^{p^m} = p^m c$, and for every $n \ge 0$ there is
$c \in \mathfrak{a}$ with $x^n - y^n = n c$.

The ring $A$ is not assumed to be torsion-free.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Lemma 25.

articles.title: Möbius sum over the divisors prime to a given prime
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, $\mu$ the Möbius
function and $n \ge 1$. The sum of $\mu(d)$ over the divisors $d$ of $n$ with $p \nmid d$ is $1$ if
$n$ is a power of $p$ (including $n = 1 = p^0$) and $0$ otherwise.

## Sources

- S. Anni, A. Ghitza and A. Medvedovsky, *Elementary Symmetric Functions and Deep Power-Sum Congruences*, INTEGERS 24 (2024), Article A46, Lemma 28.

articles.title: Coefficient denominators divide the denominator of a polynomial
articles.statement:
For every polynomial
$P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$ and every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the denominator (in lowest terms) of the
coefficient of $x^i$ in $P$ divides the denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ of $P$.

## Sources

- Bernd C. Kellner, *On the Finiteness of Bernoulli Polynomials Whose Derivative Has Only Integral Coefficients*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.2.8, Section 2 (definition of `denom`).

articles.title: Denominator one characterizes integer polynomials
articles.statement:
For every polynomial
$P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, its denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ equals $1$ if and only if, for
every $i \in \mathbb{N}$, the coefficient of $x^i$ in $P$ is an integer.

## Sources

- Bernd C. Kellner, *On the Finiteness of Bernoulli Polynomials Whose Derivative Has Only Integral Coefficients*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.2.8, Section 1 (`denom(B_n(x)) > 1` is equivalent to `B_n(x) ∉ ℤ[x]`).

articles.title: Denominator of a rational polynomial
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$, the
denominator $\operatorname{denom}(P)$ is the least common multiple of the denominators (in lowest
terms) of the nonzero coefficients of $P$; in particular $\operatorname{denom}(0) = 1$. Thus
$\operatorname{denom}(P) = 1$ exactly when $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Bernd C. Kellner, *On the Finiteness of Bernoulli Polynomials Whose Derivative Has Only Integral Coefficients*, Journal of Integer Sequences 27 (2024), Article 24.2.8, Section 2 (notation `denom`).

articles.title: Cohn's irreducibility criterion
articles.statement:
Let $b \ge 2$ be an integer and let $p$ be a prime whose
base-$b$ digits are $a_0, a_1, \dots, a_n$, with units digit $a_0$ and leading digit $a_n \ne 0$.
Then the polynomial $f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cohn%27s_irreducibility_criterion

articles.title: Dumas irreducibility criterion
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, write $v_p$ for the $p$-adic
valuation on $\mathbb{Q}$, and let $f = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ have
degree $n \ge 1$, with $a_0 \ne 0$ and $a_n \ne 0$. Suppose that no integer $k > 1$ dividing $n$
divides $v_p(a_0) - v_p(a_n)$, that is, $\gcd(v_p(a_0) - v_p(a_n), n) = 1$, and that for every
$0 \le i \le n$ with $a_i \ne 0$,
$n \, v_p(a_i) \ge (n - i) \, v_p(a_0) + i \, v_p(a_n)$.
Then $f$ is irreducible as a polynomial in $\mathbb{Q}[x]$.

Geometrically, the hypotheses say that the Newton polygon of $f$ with respect to $p$ is the single
segment from $(0, v_p(a_0))$ to $(n, v_p(a_n))$ and has no lattice points other than its
endpoints. Zero coefficients contribute no points to the Newton polygon, so the inequality is
required only for nonzero $a_i$.

## Sources

- Randell Heyman, *On the Number of Polynomials of Bounded Height that Satisfy the Dumas Criterion*, Journal of Integer Sequences 17 (2014), Article 14.2.4, Dumas criterion statement, lines 96–102, <https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL17/Heyman/heyman2.tex>. Exact algebraic form: Martin Juras, arXiv:1505.07633v1, lines 67–100.

articles.title: Mestre's square decomposition, including the quadratic case
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of
characteristic different from $2$ and let $d \ge 0$ be an integer. Every monic polynomial
$P \in K[X]$ of degree $2d + 2$ can be written as $P = Q^2 - R$ with $Q, R \in K[X]$, $Q$ monic
of degree $d + 1$ and $R$ of degree at most $d$ (possibly $R = 0$), and the pair $(Q, R)$ is
unique.

## Sources

- `mestre_monic_square_decomposition` is the source-shaped form, which assumes $d \ge 1$.

articles.title: Mestre's square decomposition
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic different from $2$
and let $d \ge 1$ be an integer. Every monic polynomial $P \in K[X]$ of degree $2d + 2$ can be
written as $P = Q^2 - R$ with $Q, R \in K[X]$, $Q$ monic of degree $d + 1$ and $R$ of degree at
most $d$ (possibly $R = 0$), and the pair $(Q, R)$ is unique.

## Sources

- Arvind Suresh, "Constructing curves of high rank via composite polynomials", arXiv:2102.02113v2, <https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.02113>, TeX lines 1158-1179, Lemma `lem:sqroot`; there coefficient comparison induces a `k`-algebra isomorphism. Follows from `mestre_monic_square_decomposition_general`; the hypothesis `hd` is unused and keeps the source's shape.

articles.title: Mixed differential along a concatenated list
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$
be an index type, let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$, and let $L$ and $L'$ be finite lists of
indices in $\sigma$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the concatenation of $L$ followed by
$L'$ equals the mixed differential along $L'$ of the mixed differential of $p$ along $L$.

articles.title: Mixed differential along a list with a given first index
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring,
let $\sigma$ be an index type, let $i \in \sigma$, let $L$ be a finite list of indices in
$\sigma$, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the list
that starts with $i$ and continues with $L$ equals the mixed differential along $L$ of
$p - \partial_i p$, where $\partial_i$ is the partial derivative with respect to $x_i$.

articles.title: The mixed differential ignores the order of the indices
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring,
let $\sigma$ be an index type, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. If two finite lists $L$ and
$L'$ of indices in $\sigma$ are permutations of each other, then the mixed differentials of $p$
along $L$ and along $L'$ are equal.

articles.title: Mixed differential along the empty list
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be
an index type, and let $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. The mixed differential of $p$ along the
empty list of indices is $p$ itself.

articles.title: Mixed differential operator
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $\sigma$ be an index
type, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial derivative with respect to $x_s$ on the polynomial
ring $R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. For a finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in $\sigma$
(repetitions allowed) and a polynomial $p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$, the mixed differential of
$p$ along the list is $(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$: the operator
$1 - \partial_{i_1}$ is applied first and $1 - \partial_{i_k}$ last. Along the empty list it is
$p$.

articles.title: Partial derivatives commute with the mixed differential
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring,
let $i \in \sigma$, let $L$ be a finite list of indices in $\sigma$, and let
$p \in R[x_s : s \in \sigma]$. Writing $\partial_i$ for the partial derivative with respect to
$x_i$, the partial derivative $\partial_i$ of the mixed differential of $p$ along $L$ equals the
mixed differential along $L$ of $\partial_i p$.

articles.title: Edge restriction to the empty set
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a
commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to the empty set, that is, the sum of the terms
of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\emptyset$, is the
zero polynomial.

articles.title: Edge restriction to the whole plane
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $f$ in two variables over a
commutative semiring $k$, the restriction of $f$ to all of $\mathbb{R}^2$, that is, the sum of the
terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\mathbb{R}^2$, is
$f$ itself.

articles.title: Restriction of a polynomial to a set of exponents
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables
over a commutative semiring $k$, and let $\Gamma \subseteq \mathbb{R}^2$. The restriction of $f$ to
$\Gamma$ is the polynomial formed by the terms of $f$ whose exponent vector, viewed as a point of
$\mathbb{R}^2$, lies in $\Gamma$; the other terms are dropped.

articles.title: Exponent vectors as points of the plane
articles.statement:
The map from exponent vectors of monomials in two
variables to $\mathbb{R}^2$ sends $e = (e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$ to the point
$(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Membership in the Newton support
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a
commutative semiring $k$. A point $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ lies in the Newton support of $f$ if and
only if $x$ is the exponent vector $e \in \mathbb{N}^2$ of some monomial with nonzero coefficient
in $f$, viewed as a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Boundary of the Newton polygon
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative
semiring $k$, the boundary of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological boundary in
$\mathbb{R}^2$: the closure of the Newton polygon minus its interior.

articles.title: The interior of the Newton polygon lies in the polygon
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $f$ in two
variables over a commutative semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ in
$\mathbb{R}^2$ is contained in the Newton polygon of $f$.

articles.title: Interior of the Newton polygon
articles.statement:
For a polynomial $f$ in two variables over a commutative
semiring $k$, the interior of the Newton polygon of $f$ is its topological interior as a subset
of $\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: The Newton polygon of the zero polynomial is empty
articles.statement:
For every commutative semiring $k$, the
Newton polygon of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of
$\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Newton polygon
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables over a commutative semiring $k$.
The Newton polygon of $f$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^2$ of the Newton support of $f$, the
set of exponent vectors of the monomials with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of
$\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: The Newton support lies in the Newton polygon
articles.statement:
For every polynomial $f$ in two variables
over a commutative semiring $k$, the Newton support of $f$ is contained in the Newton polygon of
$f$, the convex hull of the Newton support in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: The Newton support of the zero polynomial is empty
articles.statement:
For every commutative semiring $k$, the
Newton support of the zero polynomial in two variables over $k$ is the empty subset of
$\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Newton support
articles.statement:
Let $f$ be a polynomial in two variables $x_0, x_1$ over a commutative
semiring $k$. The Newton support of $f$ is the set of exponent vectors $(e_0, e_1) \in \mathbb{N}^2$
of the monomials $x_0^{e_0} x_1^{e_1}$ with nonzero coefficient in $f$, viewed as points of
$\mathbb{R}^2$.

articles.title: Partial fraction decomposition over $\mathbb{C}$
articles.statement:
For every complex rational function
$f \in \mathbb{C}(X)$ there exist a polynomial $q \in \mathbb{C}[X]$, a finite set $S$ of monic
polynomials of degree $1$ in $\mathbb{C}[X]$, and, for each $p \in S$, a natural number $m_p$
and polynomials $g_{p,k} \in \mathbb{C}[X]$ for $k < m_p$, each of degree less than the degree
of $p$, such that, in $\mathbb{C}(X)$,

$$f = q + \sum_{p \in S} \sum_{k=0}^{m_p - 1} \frac{g_{p,k}}{p^{k+1}}.$$

Only existence is stated: the standard uniqueness of the decomposition (support and
multiplicities fixed by the denominator's irreducible factors) is not, so a witness may include
polynomials $p \in S$ with $m_p = 0$ or zero numerators $g_{p,k}$.

## Sources

- S. Lang, Algebra, rev. 3rd ed., Springer, 2002, Ch. IV, §5 (Partial fractions), p. 187; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_fraction_decomposition#Statement

articles.title: Partial fraction decomposition over $\mathbb{R}$
articles.statement:
For every real rational function
$f \in \mathbb{R}(X)$ there exist a polynomial $q \in \mathbb{R}[X]$, a finite set $S$ of monic
polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[X]$, each of degree $1$ or irreducible of degree $2$, and, for each
$p \in S$, a natural number $m_p$ and polynomials $g_{p,k} \in \mathbb{R}[X]$ for $k < m_p$, each
of degree less than the degree of $p$, such that, in $\mathbb{R}(X)$,

$$f = q + \sum_{p \in S} \sum_{k=0}^{m_p - 1} \frac{g_{p,k}}{p^{k+1}}.$$

Only existence is stated: the standard uniqueness of the decomposition (support and
multiplicities fixed by the denominator's irreducible factors) is not, so a witness may include
polynomials $p \in S$ with $m_p = 0$ or zero numerators $g_{p,k}$.

## Sources

- S. Lang, Algebra, rev. 3rd ed., Springer, 2002, Ch. IV, §5 (Partial fractions), p. 187; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partial_fraction_decomposition#General_result

articles.title: Mazur–Orlicz Problem 79 has a negative answer
articles.statement:
The claim of Problem 79 of the Scottish Book
for the plane is false: there is a polynomial map $P$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ to itself with a
polynomial two-sided inverse that is not of the form $x \mapsto Ax + c$ with $A$ an invertible
real $2 \times 2$ matrix and $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$. For example, the map
$(x_1, x_2) \mapsto (x_1, x_2 + x_1^2)$ has the inverse $(y_1, y_2) \mapsto (y_1, y_2 - y_1^2)$.

## Sources

- S. Mazur and W. Orlicz, Problem 79 of the Scottish Book; typescript Ad 79 records the negative answer, via triangular polynomial automorphisms: maps `y₁ = x₁ + k`, `y₂ = x₂ + φ₂(x₁)`, …, `yₙ = xₙ + φₙ(x₁, …, xₙ₋₁)` with arbitrary polynomials `φ` are polynomial automorphisms with obvious polynomial inverses, but are not affine when some `φ` is nonlinear. For the plane, `y₁ = x₁`, `y₂ = x₂ + x₁²` already refutes affineness.

articles.title: Mazur–Orlicz claim on polynomial automorphisms of the plane
articles.statement:
The statement that every
polynomial map of the plane with a polynomial inverse is affine: for all pairs
$P = (P_1, P_2)$ and $Q = (Q_1, Q_2)$ of real polynomials in two variables such that
$Q(P(x)) = x$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$ and $P(Q(y)) = y$ for every $y \in \mathbb{R}^2$,
there are a real $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$ with $\det A \neq 0$ and a vector $c \in \mathbb{R}^2$
such that $P(x) = Ax + c$ for every $x \in \mathbb{R}^2$.

This is the affirmative answer to Mazur and Orlicz's Problem 79 of the Scottish Book,
restricted to the Euclidean plane.

articles.title: Evaluation of a regular function at a point
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a commutative semiring and let
$S$ be a commutative $k$-algebra. For a regular function $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ and a
point $a \in S^\sigma$, the evaluation of $F$ at $a$ is the point $F(a) \in S^\tau$ whose $t$-th
coordinate, for $t \in \tau$, is the value of the polynomial $F_t$ at $a$, obtained by
substituting $a_s$ for $X_s$ for every $s \in \sigma$.

articles.title: Evaluation respects composition
articles.statement:
Let $k$ be a commutative semiring and let $S$ be a
commutative $k$-algebra. For regular functions $G$ from $k^\tau$ to $k^\iota$ and $F$ from
$k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ and every point $a \in S^\sigma$, write $F(a) \in S^\tau$ for the
evaluation of $F$ at $a$. Then evaluating the composition $G \circ F$ at $a$ gives $G(F(a))$,
the evaluation of $G$ at the point $F(a)$.

articles.title: Associativity of composition of regular functions
articles.statement:
For regular functions $H$ from
$k^\iota$ to $k^\kappa$, $G$ from $k^\tau$ to $k^\iota$ and $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$,
we have $(H \circ G) \circ F = H \circ (G \circ F)$.

articles.title: The identity is a right unit for composition
articles.statement:
For every regular function $F$ from
$k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, composing $F$ with the identity regular function on $k^\sigma$, whose
components are the variables $X_s$ for $s \in \sigma$, gives $F$, that is,
$F \circ \mathrm{id} = F$.

articles.title: Composition of regular functions
articles.statement:
For regular functions $G$ from $k^\tau$ to $k^\iota$
and $F$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, the composition $G \circ F$ is the regular function from
$k^\sigma$ to $k^\iota$ whose $i$-th component, for $i \in \iota$, is the polynomial obtained
from $G_i$ by substituting $F_t$ for the variable $X_t$ for every $t \in \tau$.

articles.title: The identity is a left unit for composition
articles.statement:
For every regular function $F$ from
$k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$, composing the identity regular function on $k^\tau$, whose components
are the variables $X_t$ for $t \in \tau$, with $F$ gives $F$, that is,
$\mathrm{id} \circ F = F$.

articles.title: Jacobian matrix of a regular function
articles.statement:
The Jacobian of a regular function
$F = (F_j)_{j \in \tau}$ from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ is the $\tau \times \sigma$ matrix, with
entries in the polynomial ring $k[X_i : i \in \sigma]$, whose entry in row $j$ and column $i$ is
the formal partial derivative $\partial F_j / \partial X_i$.

Rows are indexed by the components and columns by the variables, following the usual matrix
convention, so the Jacobian multiplies column vectors indexed by $\sigma$.

articles.title: Regular functions
articles.statement:
For a commutative semiring $k$ and index types $\sigma$ and $\tau$, a
regular function from $k^\sigma$ to $k^\tau$ is a family $F = (F_t)_{t \in \tau}$ of polynomials
in the variables $X_s$, $s \in \sigma$, with coefficients in $k$.

The components are formal polynomials, not functions on $k^\sigma$.

articles.title: The auxiliary equation has a unique positive root, which exceeds $1$
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$ and
let $a$, $d$ be integers with $0 < d \le a$. Then the equation
$a x^{m+2} + (a - d) x^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) x - (a + md) = 0$ has exactly one positive real
solution, and every positive real solution $x$ satisfies $x > 1$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 1.

articles.title: Exact floors at powers of the auxiliary root (all exponents)
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$
be positive integers with $m^2 d^2 < 8a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with
$a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then
$\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor = a + pd - 1$ for every integer $p$ with $1 \le p \le m - 1$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 5, second statement.

articles.title: Exact floor at a power of the auxiliary root (single exponent)
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$,
$d$ be positive integers, and let $p$ be an integer with $1 \le p \le m - 1$ and
$p(m - p)d^2 < 2a$. If $\lambda > 0$ is a real number with
$a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$, then
$\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor = a + pd - 1$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 5.

articles.title: Strict upper bound on floors at powers of the auxiliary root
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$
be natural numbers with $d > 0$ and $(m + 1)d < 2a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with
$a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then
$\lfloor a \lambda^p \rfloor < a + pd$ for every integer $p$ with $1 \le p \le m - 1$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 4.

articles.title: The arithmetic-progression quartic is not a product of two quadratics
articles.statement:
Let $a$, $d$ be
coprime integers with $0 < d \le a$. Then the polynomial
$a x^4 + (a + d) x^3 + (a + 2d) x^2 + (a + 3d) x + (a + 4d)$ is not the product of two
polynomials of degree $2$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Theorem 4.

articles.title: Irreducibility when $d$ has a primitive-root prime factor
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$ with $m + 1$
prime, and let $a$, $d$ be coprime positive integers. Suppose $d$ has a prime divisor $p$ that is
not divisible by $m + 1$ and whose residue modulo $m + 1$ has multiplicative order $m$ (that is,
$p$ is a primitive root modulo $m + 1$). Then the polynomial
$a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + (m - 1)d) x + (a + md)$ is irreducible in
$\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 6.

articles.title: Irreducibility of polynomials with coefficients in an arithmetic progression
articles.statement:
Let
$m \ge 2$ and let $a$, $d$ be coprime positive integers with $m^2 d^2 < 8a$. Then the polynomial
$a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + (m - 1)d) x + (a + md)$ is irreducible in
$\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Theorem 2.

articles.title: Lower bound on a power of the auxiliary root
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$ be integers with
$0 < d \le a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with
$a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then
$a + md < a \lambda^m$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Lemma 2.

articles.title: The arithmetic-progression polynomial times $(x - 1)^2$
articles.statement:
For all natural numbers $m$, $a$,
$d$, the polynomial $A_m(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{m} (a + id) x^{m-i}$ satisfies, in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$,

$$A_m(x)(x - 1)^2 = a x^{m+2} - (a - d) x^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) x + (a + md).$$

The source assumes $m$, $a$, $d$ positive.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Lemma 1.

articles.title: Bound on the zeros of the arithmetic-progression polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $m \ge 2$, let $a$, $d$
be integers with $0 < d \le a$, and let $\lambda > 0$ be a real number with
$a \lambda^{m+2} + (a - d) \lambda^{m+1} - (a + (m + 1)d) \lambda - (a + md) = 0$. Then every
complex zero $z$ of $A_m(x) = a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + md)$ satisfies
$|z| \le \lambda$, and $|z| = \lambda$ only if $z = -\lambda$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Proposition 2.

articles.title: Power identity at the roots of an arithmetic-progression polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $m$ and $a$
be natural numbers, let $d$ be a positive integer, and let
$A_m(x) = a x^m + (a + d) x^{m-1} + \cdots + (a + md)$, that is,
$A_m(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{m} (a + id) x^{m-i} \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$. If $z \in \mathbb{C}$ is a root of
$A_m$ or $z = 1$, then

$$z^{m+1} = \frac{(a + (m + 1)d) z - (a + md)}{a z - (a - d)}.$$

With the paper's notation $a_n = a + (n - 1)d$ this reads
$z^{m+1} = (a_{m+2} z - a_{m+1}) / (a_1 z - a_0)$. The denominator does not vanish at such $z$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Lemma 1, equation (2).

articles.title: Reducible quadratics with coefficients in an arithmetic progression
articles.statement:
Let $d \ge 2$ be an
integer and, for a positive integer $a$, let $A_2(x) = ax^2 + (a + d)x + (a + 2d)$ in
$\mathbb{Z}[x]$. There is a positive integer $a$ coprime to $d$ for which $A_2$ is not
irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ if and only if every prime divisor of $d$ is congruent to $1$
modulo $3$. In that case the number of positive integers $a$ coprime to $d$ for which $A_2$ is
not irreducible is exactly $2^{n-1}$, where $n$ is the number of distinct prime divisors of $d$.

Both hypotheses matter: without coprimality, $a = d = 7$ gives $A_2(x) = 7(x^2 + 2x + 3)$, which
is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$; and for $d = 1$ the prime condition holds vacuously while
$A_2$ is irreducible for every $a \ge 1$, its discriminant $-3a^2 - 6a + 1$ being negative.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Theorem 3.

articles.title: A rational lower bound for $(1 + mx)^{1/m}$
articles.statement:
For every natural number $m \ge 2$ and every
real $x > 0$,

$$\frac{2 + (m + 1)x}{2 + (m - 1)x} < (1 + mx)^{1/m}.$$

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Lemma 3.

articles.title: Perron's irreducibility criterion
articles.statement:
Let $f = x^n + a_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \cdots + a_0$ be a
monic polynomial in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $n \ge 1$ with $a_0 \neq 0$ and
$|a_{n-1}| > 1 + \sum_{i=0}^{n-2} |a_i|$. Then $f$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Hiroaki Kakuma, *Irreducibility of Polynomials with Coefficients in a Positive Arithmetic Progression*, INTEGERS 26 (2026), Article A92, Theorem 1 (Perron's criterion, quoted from the paper's reference [6]).

articles.title: Even–odd decomposition of a reciprocal polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $h \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an
irreducible reciprocal polynomial of degree $2k$ such that $h \ne g(x^2)$ for every
$g \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$. Then there is exactly one $h_e \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is
exactly one $h_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one natural number $\ell$
such that $h_e$ and $h_o$ are reciprocal, $\ell$ is odd and positive, $\deg h_e = k$,
$\deg h_o = \max(k - \ell, 0)$, $h(x) = h_e(x^2) + x^\ell h_o(x^2)$ and
$h_e(0)\,h_o(0) \ne 0$.

Since $\ell$ is odd, $h_e(x^2)$ is the even part of $h$, and $h_o(0) \ne 0$ then determines
$\ell$ and $h_o$; so this amounts to a unique triple $(h_e, h_o, \ell)$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Lemma 2.1.

articles.title: Even–odd decomposition of a reciprocal 0,1-polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be
an irreducible reciprocal $0,1$-polynomial of degree $2m$ such that $f(x^2)$ is not
irreducible. Then there is exactly one $f_e \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly
one $f_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ for which there is exactly one natural number $\ell$ such that
$f_e$ and $f_o$ are reciprocal $0,1$-polynomials, $\ell$ is odd and positive,
$\deg f_e = m$, $\deg f_o = \max(m - \ell, 0)$, $f(x) = f_e(x^2) + x^\ell f_o(x^2)$ and
$f_e(0)\,f_o(0) \ne 0$.

Since $\ell$ is odd, $f_e(x^2)$ is the even part of $f$, and $f_o(0) \ne 0$ then determines
$\ell$ and $f_o$; so this amounts to a unique triple $(f_e, f_o, \ell)$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Lemma 2.2.

articles.title: Irreducibility under repeated squaring of the variable
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be
an irreducible, reciprocal, non-cyclotomic $0,1$-polynomial with fewer than $15$ nonzero
coefficients. Then $f(x^{2^n})$ is irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ for every natural
number $n$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Theorem 1.1.

articles.title: Characterization of non-cyclotomic polynomials
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is
non-cyclotomic if and only if $f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$
denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic polynomial.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: Non-cyclotomic polynomial
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is *non-cyclotomic* if
$f \ne \Phi_n$ for every positive integer $n$, where $\Phi_n$ denotes the $n$-th cyclotomic
polynomial.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: Characterization of reciprocal polynomials
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ of
degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is reciprocal if and only if its reversal
$x^d f(1/x)$ equals $f$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: Reciprocal polynomial
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_d x^d$ in
$\mathbb{Z}[x]$ of degree $d$ (with $d = 0$ for the zero polynomial) is *reciprocal*
(palindromic) if it equals its reversal $x^d f(1/x)$, that is, if $a_i = a_{d-i}$ for all
$0 \le i \le d$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: Characterization of 0,1-polynomials
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a
$0,1$-polynomial if and only if, for every $n \ge 0$, the coefficient of $x^n$ in $f$ is
$0$ or $1$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: 0,1-polynomial
articles.statement:
A polynomial $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ is a *$0,1$-polynomial* if every
coefficient of $f$ is $0$ or $1$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Section 1 (terminology).

articles.title: Position of the first odd exponent
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be an irreducible,
reciprocal, non-cyclotomic $0,1$-polynomial of degree $2m$ such that $f(x^2)$ is not
irreducible. Let $f_e, f_o \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ and let $\ell$ be a positive odd integer with
$f(x) = f_e(x^2) + x^\ell f_o(x^2)$, $\deg f_e = m$ and $\deg f_o = \max(m - \ell, 0)$, where
the degree of the zero polynomial is taken to be $0$. Then the coefficient of $x^e$ in $f$ is
$0$ for every $1 \le e < \ell$, the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in $f$ is nonzero, and $2\ell < m$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Lemma 2.3.

articles.title: Square compositions of $0,1$-polynomials modulo $4$
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be
irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, with every coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant
term $f(0) = 1$. If $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$, then
$f(x^2) \equiv f(x)\,f(-x) \pmod 4$ as polynomials, that is, the two polynomials have the
same image in $(\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z})[x]$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Theorem 1.3.

articles.title: Reducibility of $f(x^4)$ and $f(x^2)$ for $0,1$-polynomials
articles.statement:
Let
$f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and of positive degree, with every
coefficient equal to $0$ or $1$ and with constant term $f(0) = 1$. Then $f(x^4)$ is not
irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ if and only if $f(x^2)$ is not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Theorem 1.4.

articles.title: Capelli's theorem for $f(x^r)$
articles.statement:
Let $f \in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be irreducible in
$\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and let $r \ge 2$ be an integer. Then $f(x^r)$ is reducible if and only if
either $f(x^p)$ is reducible for some prime $p$ dividing $r$, or $4$ divides $r$ and
$f(x^4)$ is reducible. Here reducible means not irreducible in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$.

## Sources

- Pradipto Banerjee and Amit Kundu, "On an Irreducibility Question Concerning Palindromic Non-cyclotomic 0,1-Polynomials", Theorem 1.2 (Capelli; the root-theoretic equivalents stated there are omitted).

articles.title: Schinzel's theorem on squares of sparse polynomials
articles.statement:
The Erdős–Rényi conjecture holds:
there is a function $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$, every
complex polynomial $p$ with at least $f(k)$ nonzero coefficients has a square $p^2$ with at least
$k$ nonzero coefficients.

Schinzel (Acta Arith. 49 (1987) 55-70) proved that the number of terms of $g \in \mathbb{C}[x]$
is bounded in terms of the number of terms of $g^2$; Fuchs, Mantova and Zannier
(arXiv:1412.4548, Thm 1.1) give a uniform version.

## Sources

- C. Fuchs, V. Mantova and U. Zannier, On fewnomials, integral points and a toric version of Bertini's theorem (2017), arXiv:1412.4548, https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4548.

articles.title: Erdős–Rényi conjecture on squares of sparse polynomials
articles.statement:
There is a function
$f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$, every complex polynomial $p$
with at least $f(k)$ nonzero coefficients has a square $p^2$ with at least $k$ nonzero
coefficients.

articles.title: Symmetric polynomials in the roots are polynomials in the coefficients
articles.statement:
A symmetric polynomial is a polynomial in the elementary symmetric
polynomials, with a single witness `q` depending only on `f`; consequently,
for every monic split polynomial `P`, that same `q` evaluated at the signed
coefficients of `P` equals `f` evaluated at the roots of `P`. This is the
book's corollary that a symmetric polynomial in the roots of `P` can be
written as a polynomial in the coefficients of `P`; the signed coefficients
are the elementary symmetric polynomials in the roots, by Vieta's formulas.

articles.title: Coefficients of a weighted derivation
articles.statement: The coefficient at `g` is multiplied by the weight of `g`.

articles.title: Weighted derivation of a basis term
articles.statement: A basis term keeps its exponent and has its coefficient multiplied by the weight.

articles.title: Weighted derivation with zero weight
articles.statement: The zero weight determines the zero derivation.

articles.title: Weighted derivation of an additive monoid algebra
articles.statement: Multiply the coefficient at each exponent by an additive weight of that exponent.

articles.title: Auerbach's problem on zero sets of real polynomials
articles.statement:
Let `P` be a nonzero real polynomial in `n` variables. Its zero set does
not cut (separate) Euclidean space, i.e. the complement of the zero set is
connected, if and only if every irreducible factor of `P` over the reals is
always nonnegative or always nonpositive (as a function). The complement of
a real algebraic hypersurface is semialgebraic, so connectedness of the
complement is equivalent to the path-connectedness used by Rojas.

## Sources

- H. Auerbach, Problem 148 of the Scottish Book; both necessity and sufficiency proved by J. M. Rojas, "About Herman Auerbach's problem on factors of real polynomials with connected zero set complement", 2015 (see the commentary in Mauldin (ed.), The Scottish Book, 2nd ed., 2015).

articles.title: Nonpositivity between an upper interlacing point and the largest root
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
monic complex polynomial of positive degree all of whose roots are real, let
$\operatorname{maxroot}(p)$ be its largest root, and let $a$ be an upper interlacing point
of $p$. Then for every real $x$ with $a \le x \le \operatorname{maxroot}(p)$, the real part
of $p(x)$ is at most $0$.

articles.title: Some member's largest root is at most that of a weighted sum, via real-rooted segments
articles.statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty finite set, let $n \ge 1$, and for each $i \in I$ let $P_i$ be a monic
complex polynomial of degree $n$ and $w_i \ge 0$ a real weight. Suppose that
$Q = \sum_{i \in I} w_i P_i$ is monic of degree $n$ and that, for every $i \in I$ and every
$t \in [0, 1]$, all roots of $(1 - t) Q + t P_i$ are real. Then there is $i \in I$ with
$\operatorname{maxroot}(P_i) \le \operatorname{maxroot}(Q)$, where $\operatorname{maxroot}(f)$
denotes the largest real part of a root of $f$.

articles.title: Common upper interlacing bounds some member's largest root by a weighted sum's
articles.statement:
Let $I$
be a nonempty finite set and, for each $i \in I$, let $P_i$ be a monic complex polynomial of
positive degree all of whose roots are real, such that the family $(P_i)_{i \in I}$ has a
common upper interlacing point. Let $w_i \ge 0$ be real weights such that
$Q = \sum_{i \in I} w_i P_i$ is monic and all of its roots are real. Then there is $i \in I$
with $\operatorname{maxroot}(P_i) \le \operatorname{maxroot}(Q)$, where
$\operatorname{maxroot}(f)$ denotes the largest root of a real-rooted polynomial $f$.

articles.title: Common upper interlacing point
articles.statement:
A family $(P_i)_{i \in I}$ of complex polynomials,
indexed by an arbitrary type $I$, has a common upper interlacing point if some real number $a$
is an upper interlacing point of $P_i$ for every $i \in I$.

articles.title: Upper interlacing point
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a complex polynomial and let
$\operatorname{maxroot}(p)$ be the largest real part of an element of the multiset of roots of
$p$, with $\operatorname{maxroot}(p) = 0$ when that multiset is empty (as it is for nonzero
constants and for $p = 0$). A real number $a$ is an upper interlacing point of $p$ if
$a \le \operatorname{maxroot}(p)$ and, after removing one copy of $\operatorname{maxroot}(p)$
from the multiset of roots of $p$ (if it occurs there), every remaining root has real part at
most $a$.

articles.title: Root bound by the L1 norm
articles.statement:
Let $K$ and $L$ be fields with $L$ a $K$-algebra, let $v$ be a
real-valued absolute value on $K$, and let $w$ be a real-valued absolute value on $L$ lying over
$v$, that is, $w(x) = v(x)$ for every $x \in K$ viewed in $L$ through the algebra map. If $f$ is a
monic polynomial over $K$ and $\alpha \in L$ is a root of $f$, then $w(\alpha)$ is strictly less
than the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$.

No algebraicity, finiteness, completeness, or archimedean hypothesis is needed.

articles.title: L1 norm as a sum over the support
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute
value on $K$. For every polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$, the L1 norm $\|p\|_v$ of $p$
with respect to $v$ equals $\sum_{i \in S} v(a_i)$, where $S = \{ i : a_i \neq 0 \}$ is the
support of $p$.

articles.title: L1 norm of a monic polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a nontrivial semiring (one with $0 \neq 1$)
and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ is monic of degree
$n$, then the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$ is $\|f\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v(a_i) + 1$.

articles.title: L1 norm as a sum up to the degree
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute
value on $K$. Let $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ and let $n$ be the degree of $p$, with $n = 0$
when $p = 0$. Then the L1 norm of $p$ with respect to $v$ is $\|p\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n} v(a_i)$.

articles.title: Nonnegativity of the L1 norm
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value
on $K$. For every polynomial $p \in K[X]$, the L1 norm of $p$ with respect to $v$ satisfies
$\|p\|_v \ge 0$.

articles.title: L1 norm of the zero polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value
on $K$. The L1 norm of the zero polynomial in $K[X]$ with respect to $v$ is $0$.

articles.title: L1 norm of a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on
$K$. The L1 norm of a polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ with respect to $v$ is the real
number $\|p\|_v = \sum_i v(a_i)$, where the sum runs over the indices $i$ with $a_i \neq 0$.

articles.title: Monic polynomials close in L1 norm have the same degree
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a nontrivial ring
and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f, g \in K[x]$ are monic and the L1 norm of
$f - g$ with respect to $v$ is strictly less than $1$, then $f$ and $g$ have the same degree.

articles.title: Monic polynomials have L1 norm at least one
articles.statement:
Let $K$ be a nontrivial semiring (one with
$0 \neq 1$) and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f \in K[X]$ is monic, then the L1
norm of $f$ with respect to $v$ satisfies $\|f\|_v \ge 1$.

articles.title: Newton-type coefficient differences
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial $f = \sum_k a_k x^k$ and a
natural number $k$, $\tilde c_k(f) = (k+1)\,a_k^2 - k\,a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$, where $a_j = 0$ for $j$
above the degree of $f$; for $k = 0$ the second term vanishes, so $\tilde c_0(f) = a_0^2$.

articles.title: The parity-change bound on real zeros is false
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial
$f = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n$ of degree $n$, set $a_{n+1} = 0$, $\tilde c_0(f) = a_0^2$ and
$\tilde c_k(f) = (k+1)\,a_k^2 - k\,a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and let $v(f)$ be the
number of parity changes between consecutive terms of the increasing list of indices $k \le n$
with $\tilde c_k(f) > 0$. There is such an $f$ with $a_k > 0$ for all $0 \le k \le n$ whose number
of distinct real zeros exceeds $v(f)$.

Katkova, Shapiro and Vishnyakova (Sec. 5) disprove Conjecture 9 via iterated primitives $Q_n$ of
an explicit $Q_{15}$. Splitting the repeated root also refutes the distinct-zero reading used
here: $\prod_{j<23}(x+1+j/10^4)\,(38x^2-199x+363)$ has positive coefficients, 23 distinct real
zeros and $v = 21$.

## Sources

- Olga Katkova, Boris Shapiro and Anna Vishnyakova, In search of Newton-type inequalities, arXiv:2403.12200 (2024), https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.12200.

articles.title: Parity-change bound on real zeros (conjecture)
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial
$f = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n$ of degree $n$, set $a_{n+1} = 0$, $\tilde c_0(f) = a_0^2$ and
$\tilde c_k(f) = (k+1)\,a_k^2 - k\,a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ for $1 \le k \le n$, and let $v(f)$ be the
number of parity changes between consecutive terms of the increasing list of indices $k \le n$
with $\tilde c_k(f) > 0$. The conjecture asserts that every such $f$ with $a_k > 0$ for all
$0 \le k \le n$ has at most $v(f)$ distinct real zeros.

## Sources

- AMR-021-0014.

articles.title: Indices with positive Newton-type difference
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial
$f = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n$ of degree $n$ (with $n = 0$ for $f = 0$), set $a_{n+1} = 0$,
$\tilde c_0(f) = a_0^2$ and $\tilde c_k(f) = (k+1)\,a_k^2 - k\,a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ for $1 \le k \le n$.
This is the list of the indices $k \in \{0, \dots, n\}$ with $\tilde c_k(f) > 0$, in increasing
order.

articles.title: Parity changes of the positive-difference indices
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial
$f = a_0 + a_1 x + \dots + a_n x^n$ of degree $n$ (with $n = 0$ for $f = 0$), set $a_{n+1} = 0$,
$\tilde c_0(f) = a_0^2$ and $\tilde c_k(f) = (k+1)\,a_k^2 - k\,a_{k-1}a_{k+1}$ for $1 \le k \le n$.
Let $k_1 < k_2 < \dots < k_m$ be the indices $k \le n$ with $\tilde c_k(f) > 0$. Then $v(f)$ is the
number of $i < m$ such that $k_i$ and $k_{i+1}$ have different parities.

articles.title: For a real-rooted polynomial, the largest real part of a root is a root
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
real-rooted complex polynomial of positive degree, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of
a root of $p$. Then the real number $\rho(p)$, viewed as a complex number, is a root of $p$.

articles.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have nonnegative real part from the largest root on
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of
a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) \ge 0$ for every real
number $x \ge \rho(p)$.

articles.title: Monic real-rooted polynomials have positive real part right of the largest root
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a monic real-rooted complex polynomial, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of
a root of $p$, or $0$ if $p$ has no roots. Then $\operatorname{Re} p(x) > 0$ for every real
number $x > \rho(p)$.

articles.title: The largest real part of a root is attained
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a complex polynomial whose
multiset of roots is nonempty, and let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of a root of $p$.
Then some root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Re} z = \rho(p)$.

articles.title: Conjugation-invariant polynomials with roots in the closed lower half-plane are real-rooted
articles.statement:
