Let $p$ be a nonzero complex polynomial that is unchanged when complex conjugation is applied to
each of its coefficients. If every root $z$ of $p$ satisfies $\operatorname{Im} z \le 0$, then
$p$ is real-rooted.

articles.title: Real-rooted polynomials
articles.statement:
A complex polynomial $p$ is real-rooted if every element $z$
of its multiset of roots is real, that is, $\operatorname{Im} z = 0$.

articles.title: Largest real part of a root
articles.statement:
For a complex polynomial $p$, let $\rho(p)$ be the largest
real part $\operatorname{Re} z$ of an element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$, with
$\rho(p) = 0$ when that multiset is empty (as it is for nonzero constants and for $p = 0$).

articles.title: Real parts of roots are bounded by the largest one
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a complex polynomial and
let $\rho(p)$ be the largest real part of an element of its multiset of roots, or $0$ if that
multiset is empty. Then every element $z$ of the multiset of roots of $p$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Re} z \le \rho(p)$.

articles.title: Nonconstant complex polynomials have a root
articles.statement:
Every complex polynomial of positive
degree has at least one root.

articles.title: Partial derivatives under univariate specialization
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$p$ be a multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let
$i \in \sigma$ and $x : \sigma \to R$, and for a polynomial $q$ write $q_{i,x} \in R[X]$ for its
univariate specialization that keeps $X_i$ as the variable $X$ and sets every other $X_j$ to
$x_j$. Then $(\partial p / \partial X_i)_{i,x} = (p_{i,x})'$, the derivative of $p_{i,x}$.

articles.title: Evaluating a univariate specialization
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a
multivariate polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let
$i \in \sigma$, $x : \sigma \to R$ and $t \in R$. Evaluating at $t$ the univariate specialization
of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every other $X_j$ to $x_j$ gives $p(y)$, where
$y_i = t$ and $y_j = x_j$ for $j \ne i$.

articles.title: Real-rootedness of univariate specializations of real stable polynomials
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
real stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let
$i \in \sigma$, and for $x : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ write $p_{i,x} \in \mathbb{C}[X]$ for the
univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable $X$ and sets every other $X_j$
to $x_j$. Suppose there is a natural number $d$ such that for every $x : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$
the polynomial $p_{i,x}$ is monic of degree $d$. Then for every $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with
$a_j$ real for all $j \ne i$, the polynomial $p_{i,a}$ is real-rooted.

articles.title: Real stable polynomials
articles.statement:
A complex multivariate polynomial is real stable if it is stable
and has real coefficients.

articles.title: Stable polynomials
articles.statement:
A complex multivariate polynomial is stable if it has no zero when
every variable lies in the open upper half-plane.

articles.title: Univariate specialization at real values preserves real coefficients
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a
complex multivariate polynomial with real coefficients in variables $X_j$ indexed by
$j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $a_j$ real for every
$j \ne i$. Then the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets
every other $X_j$ to $a_j$ has real coefficients.

articles.title: The mixed differential preserves real stability
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a real stable complex
multivariate polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for
the partial derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices
in $\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list,
$(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is real stable.

articles.title: The mixed differential preserves stability
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a stable complex multivariate
polynomial in variables $X_s$ indexed by $s \in \sigma$, and write $\partial_s$ for the partial
derivative with respect to $X_s$. For every finite list $(i_1, \dots, i_k)$ of indices in
$\sigma$ (repetitions allowed, possibly empty), the mixed differential of $p$ along the list,
$(1 - \partial_{i_k}) \cdots (1 - \partial_{i_1})\, p$, is stable.

articles.title: Roots of specializations of stable polynomials lie in the closed lower half-plane
articles.statement:
Let
$p$ be a stable complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let
$i \in \sigma$, and let $a : \sigma \to \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Im} a_j \ge 0$ for every
$j \ne i$. If the univariate specialization of $p$ that keeps $X_i$ as the variable and sets every
other $X_j$ to $a_j$ is nonzero, then every root $w$ of it satisfies $\operatorname{Im} w \le 0$.

articles.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves real stability
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a real stable
complex multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$,
and write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then
$p - \partial_i p$ is real stable.

articles.title: Subtracting a partial derivative preserves stability
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a stable complex
multivariate polynomial in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, let $i \in \sigma$, and
write $\partial_i p$ for the partial derivative of $p$ with respect to $X_i$. Then
$p - \partial_i p$ is stable.

articles.title: Univariate specialization
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $p$ be a multivariate
polynomial over $R$ in variables $X_j$ indexed by $j \in \sigma$, and let $i \in \sigma$ and
$x : \sigma \to R$. The univariate specialization of $p$ at $i$ and $x$ is the polynomial in
$R[X]$ obtained from $p$ by substituting $X$ for $X_i$ and the constant $x_j$ for every $X_j$ with
$j \ne i$; the value $x_i$ is not used.

articles.title: Sturm sign-variation function
articles.statement:
For a real polynomial $p$ with Sturm chain
$p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$ and a real number $x$, $\sigma_p(x)$ is the number of sign changes,
ignoring zeros, in the sequence of values $p_0(x), p_1(x), \dots, p_m(x)$.

articles.title: Number of sign changes in a list of reals
articles.statement:
For a list $x_1, \dots, x_n$ of real numbers,
let $y_1, \dots, y_m$ be the entries of the list that are nonzero, in their original order. The
number of sign changes of the list is the number of indices $i$ with $1 \le i < m$ and
$y_i y_{i+1} < 0$, that is, the number of adjacent pairs of opposite sign once the zeros are
removed.

articles.title: Negated-remainder sequence with fuel
articles.statement:
For real polynomials $a$, $b$ and a natural
number $n$, this is the list of polynomials defined recursively by: for $n = 0$ it is the
one-entry list $(a)$; for fuel $n + 1$ it is $(a)$ if $b = 0$, and otherwise it is $a$
followed by the list for the pair $b$, $-(a \bmod b)$ with fuel $n$, where $a \bmod b$ is the
remainder of $a$ on division by $b$.

articles.title: Sturm chain
articles.statement:
The Sturm chain of a real polynomial $p$ is the list $p_0, p_1, \dots, p_m$
with $p_0 = p$, $p_1 = p'$ and $p_{k+1} = -(p_{k-1} \bmod p_k)$, the negated remainder of
$p_{k-1}$ on division by $p_k$, where the list stops at $p_m$ as soon as the next entry would
be $0$; thus $p_m$ is its last entry and, for $p \ne 0$, every entry is nonzero. For $p = 0$
the chain is the one-entry list $(0)$.

articles.title: Sturm's theorem
articles.statement:
Let $p$ be a squarefree real polynomial and let $a < b$ be real numbers
with $p(a) \ne 0$ and $p(b) \ne 0$. Then the number of distinct real roots $x$ of $p$ with
$a < x < b$ equals $\sigma_p(a) - \sigma_p(b)$, where $\sigma_p$ is the Sturm sign-variation
function of $p$ and the subtraction is truncated subtraction of natural numbers.

## Sources

- J. C. F. Sturm (1829). Listed as §97 in O. Knill, Some Fundamental Theorems in Mathematics (https://people.math.harvard.edu/~knill/graphgeometry/papers/fundamental.pdf). Formalized in Isabelle/HOL by Manuel Eberl (AFP entry Sturm_Sequences). Problem `sturm` of the lean-eval benchmark.

articles.title: Double root criterion
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and
let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. Then $f(a) = 0$ and $f'(a) = 0$ if and only if
$f = (x - a)^2 g$ for some $g \in R[x]$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 9.13.

articles.title: First-order Taylor expansion of a polynomial
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$f \in R[X]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. There is a unique
polynomial $g \in R[X]$ such that

$$f = f(a) + f'(a)\,(X - a) + g\,(X - a)^2.$$

articles.title: A nonvanishing derivative excludes a double root
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. If $f'(a) \neq 0$,
then $(x - a)^2$ does not divide $f$ in $R[x]$.

No assumption on $f(a)$ is needed.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, consequence of Corollary 9.13.

articles.title: Double root criterion in divisibility form
articles.statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let
$f \in R[x]$ and $a \in R$, and let $f'$ be the formal derivative of $f$. Then $(x - a)^2$
divides $f$ in $R[x]$ if and only if $f(a) = 0$ and $f'(a) = 0$.

## Sources

- ATLAS NumberTheoryI, Corollary 9.13.
